description: Kubernetes 1.31 'Elli' brings 45 enhancements with a focus on security and networking. AppArmor support graduates to GA after 8 years, nftables kube-proxy moves to beta, and pod failure policy reaches stable. This release also introduces OCI artifacts as volume sources (alpha) and improves consistent reads from cache.

actionRequired.description: Kubelet flag `--keep-terminated-pod-volumes` was removed.  This flag was deprecated in 2017.
actionRequired.author: carlory

enrichment.title: Remove deprecated kubelet flag
enrichment.summary: The kubelet flag `--keep-terminated-pod-volumes` has been removed.
enrichment.action: Delete the `--keep-terminated-pod-volumes` flag from all kubelet startup configurations and ensure any custom handling of terminated pod volumes is updated.

actionRequired.description:
Added support to the scheduler to start using QueueingHint registered for Pod/Updated event to determine whether unschedulable Pods update make them schedulable, when the feature gate `SchedulerQueueingHints` is enabled.
Previously, when unschedulable Pods are updated, the scheduler always put Pods back to activeQ/backoffQ. But, actually not all updates to Pods make Pods schedulable, especially considering many scheduling constraints nowadays are immutable.
Now, when unschedulable Pods are updated, the scheduling queue checks with QueueingHint(s) whether the update may make the pods schedulable, and requeues them to activeQ/backoffQ **only when** at least one QueueingHint(s) return Queue. 

Action required for custom scheduler plugin developers:
Plugins **have to** implement a QueueingHint for Pod/Update event if the rejection from them could be resolved by updating unscheduled Pods themselves.
Example: suppose you develop a custom plugin that denies Pods that have a `schedulable=false` label. 
Given Pods with a `schedulable=false` label will be schedulable if the `schedulable=false` label is removed, this plugin would implement QueueingHint for Pod/Update event that returns Queue when such label changes are made in unscheduled Pods.
actionRequired.author: AxeZhan

enrichment.title: Add QueueingHint support for pod updates
enrichment.summary: Scheduler now uses QueueingHint for Pod/Update events (when SchedulerQueueingHints feature gate is enabled) to decide if updated unschedulable Pods should be requeued.
enrichment.action: If you develop custom scheduler plugins, implement a QueueingHint for the Pod/Update event to return Queue when an update can make a previously rejected Pod schedulable.

actionRequired.description: Removed admission plugin `PersistentVolumeLabel`. Please use https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cloud-pv-admission-labeler instead if you need a similar functionality.
actionRequired.author: jsafrane

enrichment.title: Remove PersistentVolumeLabel admission plugin
enrichment.summary: The admission plugin `PersistentVolumeLabel` has been removed from the API server.
enrichment.action: Delete `PersistentVolumeLabel` from the API server admission plugin list and, if needed, deploy the cloud-pv-admission-labeler webhook to provide similar functionality.

actionRequired.description: CephFS volume plugin ( `kubernetes.io/cephfs`) was removed in this release and the `cephfs` volume type became non-functional. Alternative is to use CephFS CSI driver (https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/) in your Kubernetes Cluster. A re-deployment of your application is required to use the new driver if you were using `kubernetes.io/cephfs` volume plugin before upgrading cluster version to 1.31+.
actionRequired.author: carlory

enrichment.title: Remove in‑tree CephFS volume plugin
enrichment.summary: The in‑tree CephFS volume plugin (`kubernetes.io/cephfs`) was removed, making the `cephfs` volume type non‑functional.
enrichment.action: Deploy the CephFS CSI driver, update manifests to use the CSI driver instead of `kubernetes.io/cephfs`, and redeploy any applications that used the removed plugin.

actionRequired.description: CephRBD volume plugin ( `kubernetes.io/rbd`) was removed in this release. And its csi migration support was also removed, so the `rbd` volume type became non-functional. Alternative is to use RBD CSI driver (https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/) in your Kubernetes Cluster. A re-deployment of your application is required to use the new driver if you were using `kubernetes.io/rbd` volume plugin before upgrading cluster version to 1.31+.
actionRequired.author: carlory

enrichment.title: Remove in‑tree CephRBD volume plugin
enrichment.summary: The in‑tree CephRBD volume plugin (`kubernetes.io/rbd`) was removed, making the `rbd` volume type non‑functional and dropping its CSI migration support.
enrichment.action: Install the RBD CSI driver, modify manifests to use the CSI driver instead of `kubernetes.io/rbd`, and redeploy any workloads that relied on the removed plugin.

actionRequired.description:
Improved scheduling performance when many nodes, and prefilter returned 1-2 nodes (e.g. daemonset)

For developers of out-of-tree PostFilter plugins, note that the semantics of NodeToStatusMap are changing: A node with an absent value in the NodeToStatusMap should be interpreted as having an UnschedulableAndUnresolvable status.
actionRequired.author: gabesaba

enrichment.title: NodeToStatusMap semantics change for PostFilter plugins
enrichment.summary: Scheduler performance was improved for large clusters, and the semantics of NodeToStatusMap in out‑of‑tree PostFilter plugins now treat missing entries as UnschedulableAndUnresolvable.
enrichment.action: Update any custom PostFilter plugins to interpret absent nodes in NodeToStatusMap as having an UnschedulableAndUnresolvable status.

actionRequired.description:
Reduced state change noise when volume expansion fails. Also mark certain failures as infeasible.

ACTION REQUIRED:  If you are using the `RecoverVolumeExpansionFailure` alpha feature gate
then after upgrading to this release, you need to update some objects.
For any existing PersistentVolumeClaimss with `status.allocatedResourceStatus` set to either
"ControllerResizeFailed" or "NodeResizeFailed", clear the `status.allocatedResourceStatus`.
actionRequired.author: gnufied

enrichment.title: Clear PVC allocatedResourceStatus after volume expansion failure
enrichment.summary: State change noise on failed volume expansions is reduced and some failures are now marked infeasible; users of the RecoverVolumeExpansionFailure feature must clear specific PVC statuses.
enrichment.action: For all PVCs that have `status.allocatedResourceStatus` set to "ControllerResizeFailed" or "NodeResizeFailed", clear that field after upgrading when the RecoverVolumeExpansionFailure alpha gate is enabled.

actionRequired.description:
ACTION REQUIRED for custom scheduler plugin developers:
`EventsToRegister` in the `EnqueueExtensions` interface gets `ctx` in the parameters and `error` in the return values.
Please change your plugins' implementation accordingly.
actionRequired.author: googs1025

enrichment.title: Update EnqueueExtensions.EventsToRegister signature
enrichment.summary: The `EventsToRegister` method in the `EnqueueExtensions` interface now takes a context parameter and returns an error.
enrichment.action: Modify any custom scheduler plugins to add a `ctx` argument to `EventsToRegister` and handle the returned `error` in the method implementation.

securityInformation.title: Nodes can delete themselves by adding an OwnerReference
securityInformation.description: A vulnerability exists in the NodeRestriction admission controller where node users can delete their corresponding node object by patching themselves with an OwnerReference to a cluster-scoped resource. If the OwnerReference resource does not exist or is subsequently deleted, the given node object will be deleted via garbage collection. By default, node users are authorized for create and patch requests but not delete requests against their node object. Since the NodeRestriction admission controller does not prevent patching OwnerReferences, a compromised node could leverage this vulnerability to delete and then recreate its node object with modified taints or labels.

securityInformation.title: Node Denial of Service via Kubelet Checkpoint API
securityInformation.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a large number of container checkpoint requests made to the unauthenticated kubelet read-only HTTP endpoint may cause a Node Denial of Service by filling the Node's disk.

securityInformation.title: Command Injection affecting Windows nodes via nodes/*/logs/query API
securityInformation.description:
A security vulnerability has been discovered in Kubernetes windows nodes
that could allow a user with the ability to query a node's '/logs' endpoint
to execute arbitrary commands on the host.

feature.description:
Added support for building Windows kube-proxy container image.
A container image for kube-proxy on Windows can now be built with the command
`make release-images KUBE_BUILD_WINDOWS=y`.
The Windows kube-proxy image can be used with Windows Host Process Containers.
feature.author: claudiubelu
feature.userFacingChange:
Added support for building Windows kube-proxy container image.
A container image for kube-proxy on Windows can now be built with the command
`make release-images KUBE_BUILD_WINDOWS=y`.
The Windows kube-proxy image can be used with Windows Host Process Containers.

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes did not provide a way to build a container image for kube-proxy on Windows, preventing clusters that use Windows Host Process Containers from deploying the proxy component.
enrichment.affected: Users running Windows nodes that need kube-proxy, especially those using Windows Host Process Containers.
enrichment.fix: Added a build option (`make release-images KUBE_BUILD_WINDOWS=y`) that produces a Windows‑compatible kube-proxy container image. The image can be used directly with Windows Host Process Containers.
enrichment.impact: Enables Windows workloads to have kube-proxy for service IP routing and network traffic distribution, simplifying cluster setup and reducing the need for custom builds.

feature.description:
kube-scheduler implemented scheduling hints for the CSILimit plugin.
The scheduling hints allow the scheduler to retry scheduling a Pod that was previously rejected by the CSILimit plugin if a deleted pod has a PersistantVolumeClaim (PVC) from the same driver.
feature.author: utam0k
feature.userFacingChange:
kube-scheduler implements scheduling hints for the CSILimit plugin.
The scheduling hints allow the scheduler to retry scheduling a Pod that was previously rejected by the CSILimit plugin if a deleted pod has a PVC from the same driver.

enrichment.problem: When a pod was rejected by the CSILimit scheduler plugin because the driver appeared to have reached its PVC limit, the scheduler did not retry the pod after a previously scheduled pod using a PVC from the same driver was deleted, leaving the pod pending despite freed capacity.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use CSI drivers with PVC limits, especially those scheduled after a previous pod with a PVC from the same driver was deleted.
enrichment.fix: kube-scheduler now provides scheduling hints to the CSILimit plugin. If a pod is rejected due to PVC limits, the scheduler can retry the pod when a deleted pod’s PVC from the same CSI driver frees up capacity, allowing the pod to be scheduled successfully.
enrichment.impact: Pods that were incorrectly stuck in Pending due to stale CSI limit rejections can now be scheduled promptly, improving workload reliability and storage resource utilization.

feature.description:
This PR added tracing support to the kubelet's read-only endpoint, which currently
does not have tracing. It makes use of the `WithPublicEndpoint` option to prevent callers
from influencing sampling decisions.
feature.author: frzifus
feature.userFacingChange: This PR adds tracing support to the kubelet's read-only endpoint, which currently does not have tracing. It makes use the WithPublicEndpoint option to prevent callers from influencing sampling decisions.

issueContext.title: Add Tracing to the kubelet's read-only endpoint
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Follow-up to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/105126.  Discussed in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/105126#discussion_r783142176.

As part of kubelet tracing beta, we should add tracing support to the kubelet's read-only endpoint, which currently does not have tracing.  It should use WithPublicEndpoint to prevent callers from influencing sampling decisions.

### Why is this needed?

Part of https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/2831

enrichment.problem: The kubelet's read‑only HTTP endpoint did not emit OpenTelemetry traces, so calls to this endpoint could not be observed or correlated with other cluster activity. Callers could also affect sampling decisions, leading to inconsistent tracing data.
enrichment.affected: Any component or client that calls the kubelet's read‑only endpoint (e.g., monitoring agents, kubectl, kube‑proxy health checks) now receives tracing data.
enrichment.fix: Implemented tracing for the read‑only endpoint by instrumenting the handler and using the WithPublicEndpoint option, which isolates sampling decisions from external callers.
enrichment.impact: Operators and tooling can now trace requests to the kubelet's read‑only endpoint, improving debugging, performance analysis, and overall observability of node‑level interactions.

feature.description: If the feature-gate VolumeAttributesClass is enabled, when finding a suitable persistent volume for a claim, the kube-controller-manager will be aware of the `volumeAttributesClassName` field of PVC and PV objects. The `volumeAttributesClassName` field is a reference to a VolumeAttributesClass object, which contains a set of key-value pairs that present mutable attributes of the volume. It's forbidden to change the `volumeAttributesClassName` field of a PVC object until the PVC is bound to a PV object. During the binding process, if a PVC has a `volumeAttributesClassName` field set, the controller will only consider volumes that have the same `volumeAttributesClassName` as the PVC. If the `volumeAttributesClassName` field is not set or set to an empty string, only volumes with empty `volumeAttributesClassName` will be considered.
feature.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: When the VolumeAttributesClass feature gate is enabled, the controller manager did not consider the `volumeAttributesClassName` field on PVCs and PVs during binding, potentially binding claims to volumes with mismatched mutable attributes.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with the VolumeAttributesClass feature gate enabled and workloads that use PVCs specifying `volumeAttributesClassName`.
enrichment.fix: The kube‑controller‑manager now reads the `volumeAttributesClassName` field on PVC and PV objects during the binding process. It only matches PVs whose `volumeAttributesClassName` matches the PVC (or both are empty) when the field is set.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that PersistentVolumeClaims are bound to volumes that share the specified mutable attribute class, preventing incorrect volume assignments and improving predictability for users leveraging VolumeAttributesClass.

feature.description: kube-apiserver: Added support to disable http/2 serving with a `--disable-http2-serving` flag.
feature.author: slashpai
feature.userFacingChange: kube-apiserver: http/2 serving can be disabled with a `--disable-http2-serving` flag

enrichment.problem: Kube-apiserver always served HTTP/2, providing no way to disable it, which could cause compatibility or debugging issues for environments that require HTTP/1.1 only.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where the apiserver is accessed by clients that cannot handle HTTP/2 or where HTTP/2 is undesired.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new `--disable-http2-serving` flag for kube-apiserver that, when set, disables HTTP/2 serving and falls back to HTTP/1.1.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators can now opt‑out of HTTP/2 when needed, improving compatibility with legacy clients or specific network configurations and simplifying troubleshooting of protocol‑related issues.
