issueContext.title: Improve how to move Pods when Pods are updated
issueContext.body:
Currently when the Pod, which is in the unschedQ is updated, that Pod is moved to activeQ/backoffQ.
But, not all changes actually make the Pod schedulable. So, it's worth determining if the update of Pod makes the Pod schedulable or not by QueueingHint.

Context: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119607#discussion_r1349241537

enrichment.problem: When unschedulable Pods are updated, the scheduler always moved them back to the active or backoff queue, even if the update could not make them schedulable. This caused unnecessary scheduling cycles, especially because many scheduling constraints are immutable.
enrichment.affected: Pods that are unschedulable and receive an update; custom scheduler plugin developers whose plugins reject Pods based on mutable criteria.
enrichment.fix: With the SchedulerQueueingHints feature gate enabled, the scheduler consults QueueingHint implementations registered for the Pod/Update event. Only if at least one hint returns **Queue** does the pod get re‑queued to active/backoff. Custom scheduler plugins must now provide a QueueingHint for updates that could resolve their own rejections.
enrichment.impact: Reduces wasted scheduling attempts and improves scheduler efficiency. Custom plugin developers must add QueueingHint logic to keep their plugins functional under the new behavior.

feature.description:
The kube-scheduler added scheduling hints for the InterPodAffinity plugin.
These hints allow the scheduler to retry scheduling a Pod
that was previously rejected by the InterPodAffinity plugin if there are changes (create, delete, or update) to a related Pod or a node that matches the pod affinity criteria.
feature.author: nayihz
feature.userFacingChange:
kube-scheduler implements scheduling hints for the InterPodAffinity plugin.
The scheduling hints allow the scheduler to retry scheduling a Pod
that was previously rejected by the InterPodAffinity plugin if create/delete/update a related Pod or a node which matches the pod affinity.

enrichment.problem: When a Pod was rejected by the InterPodAffinity plugin, the scheduler would not retry scheduling it even after related Pods or Nodes changed to satisfy the affinity rules, causing Pods to remain unschedulable.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that use InterPodAffinity (e.g., Pods with required or preferred podAffinity/antiAffinity) could be blocked from scheduling until a manual delete/recreate. After the change, they are automatically retried when the environment changes.
enrichment.fix: Implemented scheduling hints for the InterPodAffinity plugin. The scheduler now records a hint on rejection and will re‑evaluate the Pod when a related Pod is created, updated, or deleted, or when a Node matching the affinity criteria changes, allowing the Pod to be scheduled without manual intervention.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on inter‑pod affinity can now be scheduled automatically as soon as the required affinity conditions become true, reducing scheduling failures and operational overhead for users.

feature.description: Implemented new cluster events UpdatePodScaleDown and UpdatePodLabel for scheduler plugins.
feature.author: sanposhiho
feature.userFacingChange: Implement new cluster events UpdatePodScaleDown and UpdatePodLabel for scheduler plugins.

enrichment.problem: Scheduler plugins had no way to be notified when a pod was scaled down or when its labels changed, limiting their ability to adjust scheduling decisions based on these events.
enrichment.affected: Custom scheduler plugins and any workloads that rely on plugin reactions to pod scale‑down or label updates.
enrichment.fix: Introduced two new cluster events, UpdatePodScaleDown and UpdatePodLabel, that are emitted by the kube-scheduler and can be consumed by scheduler plugins.
enrichment.impact: Plugins can now react to pod scale‑down and label changes, enabling more dynamic and accurate scheduling logic for custom or built‑in plugins.

feature.description:
Added the `WatchList` method to the `rest client` in `client-go`. When used,
it establishes a stream to obtain a consistent snapshot of data from the server.
This method is meant to be used by the generated client.
feature.author: p0lyn0mial
feature.userFacingChange: Add the` WatchList` method to the `rest client` in `client-go`. When used, it establishes a stream to obtain a consistent snapshot of data from the server. This method is meant to be used by the generated client.

enrichment.problem: Generated client code had no way to request a consistent snapshot of resources via a watch list, forcing callers to implement ad‑hoc logic or suffer from potential data inconsistency.
enrichment.affected: Developers using client‑go generated clients (e.g., custom controllers, operators) that need a consistent snapshot of resources via watch.
enrichment.fix: Added a new `WatchList` method to the `rest.Interface` in client‑go. The method opens a watch stream that returns an initial list (the snapshot) followed by incremental watch events, providing a consistent view of the server state. It is intended for use by code generated by client‑go.
enrichment.impact: Clients generated by client‑go can now obtain a reliable initial state and subsequent updates in a single operation, simplifying controller implementations and improving correctness of watch‑based reconciliation loops.

feature.description: Added support for kube-proxy iptables mode to track packets that were wrongfully marked invalid by conntrack and subsequently dropped by introducing `kubeproxy_iptables_ct_state_invalid_dropped_packets_total` metric.
feature.author: aroradaman
feature.userFacingChange: The iptables mode of kube-proxy now tracks packets that are wrongfully marked invalid by conntrack and subsequently dropped by introducing `kubeproxy_iptables_ct_state_invalid_dropped_packets_total` metric

enrichment.problem: When using kube-proxy in iptables mode, packets that conntrack incorrectly marks as INVALID are silently dropped, providing no visibility into potential network issues.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using kube-proxy in iptables mode; any pods or services whose traffic may be impacted by conntrack's mis‑classification of packets.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the metric `kubeproxy_iptables_ct_state_invalid_dropped_packets_total` which counts packets dropped after being marked INVALID by conntrack, allowing operators to monitor and diagnose these events.
enrichment.impact: Operators of clusters that run kube-proxy in iptables mode can now observe and alert on unexpected packet drops, improving troubleshooting of network connectivity problems.

feature.description: Fixed a missing behavior where Windows nodes did not implement memory-pressure eviction.
feature.author: marosset

enrichment.problem: Windows nodes were missing the memory‑pressure eviction behavior, so pods were not evicted when the node experienced memory pressure.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that run Windows worker nodes; any pods scheduled on those nodes could be affected by uncontrolled memory pressure.
enrichment.fix: Implemented the memory‑pressure eviction logic for Windows nodes, aligning their behavior with Linux nodes.
enrichment.impact: Prevents OOM situations on Windows nodes, ensures stable workloads, and makes node resource management consistent across OSes.

feature.description: kubelet: warn instead of error for the unsupported options on Windows "CgroupsPerQOS" and "EnforceNodeAllocatable".
feature.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: Kubelet treated the Windows‑specific options CgroupsPerQOS and EnforceNodeAllocatable as errors, causing kubelet startup failures on Windows nodes that had these unsupported settings.
enrichment.affected: Windows nodes running kubelet with CgroupsPerQOS or EnforceNodeAllocatable set (usually default or user‑specified configurations).
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now logs these unsupported options as warnings instead of errors, allowing the service to start and continue operating on Windows nodes.
enrichment.impact: Windows nodes no longer become NotReady or fail to start due to these options, improving cluster stability and reducing manual remediation for Windows workloads.

feature.description:
Added `--keep-*` flags to `kubectl debug`, which enables to control the removal
of probes, labels, annotations and initContainers from copy pod.
feature.author: mochizuki875
feature.userFacingChange: Add `--keep-*` flags to `kubectl debug`, which enables to control the removal of probes, labels, annotations and initContainers from copy pod.

enrichment.problem: When using `kubectl debug`, the tool automatically stripped probes, labels, annotations, and initContainers from the copy pod, causing loss of important metadata and requiring extra manual steps to restore them for debugging.
enrichment.affected: Users who invoke `kubectl debug` and need to retain probes, labels, annotations, or init containers on the debug copy pod.
enrichment.fix: Introduced `--keep-probes`, `--keep-labels`, `--keep-annotations`, and `--keep-initcontainers` flags to allow users to preserve those fields in the debug copy pod.
enrichment.impact: Users can now debug pods without losing essential configuration, saving time and reducing the risk of mis‑debugging due to missing probes or init containers. Improves flexibility and usability of the debugging workflow.

feature.description: Graduated support for Container Device Interface (CDI) device IDs to general availability. The `DevicePluginCDIDevices` feature gate is now enabled unconditionally.
feature.author: bart0sh
feature.userFacingChange: Graduated support for CDI device IDs to general availability. The `DevicePluginCDIDevices` feature gate is now enabled unconditionally.

enrichment.problem: Support for Container Device Interface (CDI) device IDs was gated behind the DevicePluginCDIDevices feature flag, requiring users to manually enable it before using CDI device IDs.
enrichment.affected: Users of device plugins that rely on CDI device IDs, and any workloads that need those device IDs, were required to enable a feature gate; now they work by default.
enrichment.fix: The DevicePluginCDIDevices feature gate is now enabled unconditionally, graduating CDI device ID support to general availability.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now use CDI device IDs out‑of‑the‑box without extra configuration, simplifying device plugin development and improving workload portability across nodes.

feature.description: The PodDisruptionBudget `spec.unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy` field has graduated to GA. This field may be set to `AlwaysAllow` to always allow unhealthy pods covered by the PodDisruptionBudget to be evicted.
feature.author: atiratree

enrichment.problem: Before GA, the PodDisruptionBudget field `spec.unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy` was not generally available, limiting operators' ability to control eviction of unhealthy pods during voluntary disruptions.
enrichment.affected: Users managing workloads with PodDisruptionBudgets who need to evict unhealthy pods during maintenance or scaling events.
enrichment.fix: The field has graduated to GA, allowing it to be set to `AlwaysAllow` so that unhealthy pods covered by a PDB can be evicted regardless of their health status.
enrichment.impact: Enables more predictable and flexible disruption handling for workloads using PDBs, reducing potential bottlenecks where unhealthy pods block voluntary evictions.

feature.description: Moved `ConsistentListFromCache` feature flag to beta and enabled it by default.
feature.author: serathius
feature.userFacingChange: Move ConsistentListFromCache feature flag to Beta and enable it by default

enrichment.problem: The ConsistentListFromCache feature was only available as an alpha flag and disabled by default, causing users to miss out on consistent list responses and the performance benefits of serving list requests from the cache.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the Kubernetes API server, especially workloads that rely on frequent LIST calls (e.g., controllers, operators).
enrichment.fix: Promoted the ConsistentListFromCache feature flag to beta and enabled it by default, so the API server now serves list calls from the cache consistently unless explicitly turned off.
enrichment.impact: Improves the consistency of list operations and reduces load on the storage backend for all clusters, providing better performance and reliability without requiring user intervention.

feature.description: CEL: added name formats library.
feature.author: alexzielenski
feature.userFacingChange: CEL: add name formats library

enrichment.problem: Before this change, there was no shared library of name‑format functions for Common Expression Language (CEL) used in API validation. Developers had to implement their own regex or string checks, leading to duplicated logic, harder maintenance, and potential inconsistencies in resource name validation.
enrichment.affected: Users writing custom admission/webhook validation rules or KEPs that rely on CEL expressions for name validation; cluster operators who depend on consistent resource naming checks.
enrichment.fix: Introduce a new CEL name‑formats library that provides built‑in functions for common Kubernetes naming conventions (DNS‑1123, DNS‑1123‑subdomain, label names, etc.). The library is registered with the CEL runtime used by the apiserver, so validation rules can reference these functions directly.
enrichment.impact: API developers can write more concise and reliable CEL validation rules without re‑implementing name checks. This reduces bugs, streamlines admission control policies, and improves consistency across resources that enforce naming constraints.

feature.description: Added `cri-client` staging repository.
feature.author: saschagrunert

enrichment.problem: There was no dedicated staging repository for the cri-client library, making it harder for developers to build and test the CRI client code.
enrichment.affected: Developers and CI pipelines that need the CRI client library for building or testing components such as kubelet or node‑related tools.
enrichment.fix: A new `cri-client` staging repository has been added, providing a place to store and develop the CRI client code separate from the main repositories.
enrichment.impact: Developers and SIGs that depend on the CRI client (e.g., kubelet, testing frameworks) can now more easily access, build, and contribute to the library, improving development workflow and CI testing for CRI-related features.

feature.description:
Services implemented a field selector for the ClusterIP and Type fields.
The Kubelet uses this field selector to avoid monitoring Headless Services, which helps reduce memory consumption.
feature.author: aojea
feature.userFacingChange:
Services implement a field selector for the ClusterIP and Type fields.
Kubelet uses the fieldselector on Services to avoid watching for Headless Services and reduce the memory consumption.

issueContext.title: Support skip watch Headless Service in server-side.
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Support watch service with field-selector spec.clusterIP!=None to skip headless service in kube-apiserver. And kubelet/kube-proxy can skip watch headless-service in the future.
![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/42128207/55a3df12-e70d-4b09-b5a4-a5a6ebff890e)

Now, endpoints will be added labels [service.kubernetes.io/headless](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/endpoint/endpoints_controller.go#L518) for headless service  by endpoints-controller,  and kube-proxy will ignore  event for it by label-selector. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go#L913. But headless service haven't be added label and kube-proxy  still watch for it.

For kubelet, it watch service to add service-env for pods , but it ignores headless service when  build service-env-map(https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L549). So kubelet don't need to watch headless service either.

### Why is this needed?

In a large-cluster with more then 5000 nodes,  when we run kubeflow task( tfjob:pod:headlessService=1:10:10) with qps 10, it can save huge network bandwidth and cpu for kube-apiserver.

enrichment.problem: Kubelet (and the API server) watched all Service objects, including headless Services, causing unnecessary memory consumption and watch traffic, especially in large clusters with many headless Services.
enrichment.affected: kubelet nodes that watch Services; clusters with a high number of headless Services; indirectly the API server handling Service watches.
enrichment.fix: Implemented a field selector for Services on the spec.clusterIP and spec.type fields. Kubelet now uses the selector (spec.clusterIP!=None) to exclude headless Services from its watch stream, reducing memory usage.
enrichment.impact: Reduces kubelet memory footprint and watch bandwidth, improving scalability and performance of large clusters that run many headless Services.

feature.description:
Added apiserver.latency.k8s.io/apf-queue-wait annotation to the audit log
to record the time spent waiting in APF queue.
feature.author: hakuna-matatah
feature.userFacingChange: Add apiserver.latency.k8s.io/apf-queue-wait annotation to the audit log to record the time spent waiting in apf queue

enrichment.problem: Audit logs did not capture how long a request spent waiting in the APF (API Priority and Fairness) queue, making it hard to diagnose latency caused by request throttling.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the audit logging feature, especially those with heavy API traffic or enabled APF, will now see an additional annotation in audit records.
enrichment.fix: Added the apiserver.latency.k8s.io/apf-queue-wait annotation to audit log entries, recording the duration each request waited in the APF queue.
enrichment.impact: Operators and developers gain visibility into APF‑induced latency, enabling better performance debugging and capacity planning for API server traffic.

feature.description: Continued streaming kubelet logs when the CRI server of the runtime was unavailable.
feature.author: saschagrunert
feature.userFacingChange: Continue streaming kubelet logs when the CRI server of the runtime is unavailable.

enrichment.problem: When the container runtime's CRI server became unavailable, kubelet stopped streaming container logs, causing gaps in log continuity for affected pods.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where kubelet streams container logs and the underlying CRI runtime becomes temporarily unavailable. Pods running on those nodes may have experienced missing logs.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet was updated to continue streaming logs even if the CRI server cannot be reached, ensuring log flow remains uninterrupted during runtime outages.
enrichment.impact: Operators retain continuous observability of pod logs during transient CRI failures, improving debugging and reducing uncertainty about container activity.

feature.description:
- Windows Kubeproxy will use the update load balancer API for load balancer updates, instead of the previous delete and create APIs.
- Deletion of remote endpoints will be triggered only for terminated endpoints (those present in the old endpoints map but not in the new endpoints map), whereas previously it was also done for terminating endpoints.
feature.author: princepereira
feature.userFacingChange:
- Windows Kubeproxy will use the update load balancer API for load balancer updates, instead of the previous delete and create APIs.
- Deletion of remote endpoints will be triggered only for terminated endpoints (those present in the old endpoints map but not in the new endpoints map), whereas previously it was also done for terminating endpoints.

enrichment.problem: Windows kube-proxy previously updated service load balancers by deleting and recreating them, and it removed remote endpoints for both terminating and terminated endpoints, causing unnecessary load balancer churn and potential brief service disruptions.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running Windows nodes with kube-proxy enabled; specifically, services that rely on load balancer updates on Windows.
enrichment.fix: Switch Windows kube-proxy to use the load balancer *update* API instead of delete/create, and limit remote endpoint deletions to only terminated endpoints (those present in the old map but missing from the new map).
enrichment.impact: Reduces load balancer operations and avoids unnecessary endpoint deletions, leading to more stable service updates and lower load on cloud provider APIs for Windows clusters.

feature.description: Kubemark: added two flags, `--kube-api-qps` which indicates the maximum QPS to the apiserver, and `--kube-api-burst` which indicates maximum burst for throttle to the apiserver.
feature.author: devincd
feature.userFacingChange: Kubemark: adds two flags, `--kube-api-qps` and `--kube-api-burst`

enrichment.problem: Kubemark could not configure the client-side request rate to the apiserver, so tests were forced to use default QPS and burst limits which could cause unintended throttling or unrealistic load patterns.
enrichment.affected: Users running Kubemark for scalability testing of large Kubernetes clusters; test environments that need to simulate specific API request rates.
enrichment.fix: Introduced two new command‑line flags, `--kube-api-qps` and `--kube-api-burst`, allowing users to set the maximum queries‑per‑second and burst size for API requests made by Kubemark.
enrichment.impact: Enables more precise control of API traffic in scalability tests, preventing unwanted throttling and producing more realistic performance results for large‑cluster simulations.

feature.description: Add a TopologyManager policy option: max-allowable-numa-nodes to configures maxAllowableNUMANodes for kubelet.
feature.author: cyclinder

issueContext.title: Make maxAllowableNUMANodes in the kubelet's TopologyManager configurable
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Add a config option to the `kubelet` that allows us to configure the value of `maxAllowableNUMANodes` in the TopologyManager:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/79c61d5f0305c566b642be978b1e4837870db257/pkg/kubelet/cm/topologymanager/topology_manager.go#L40

### Why is this needed?

The current hard-coded value of 8 was added as a stop-gap 4 years ago, with a plan to improve the topology manager to remove the state explosion that occurs when trying to enumerate the possible NUMA affinities and generating their hints (which unfortunately never happened).

The long term solution should be to refactor this code to avoid the state explosion altogether. In the meantime, a configurable option should be sufficient to allow users to increase the limit when appropriate.

enrichment.problem: TopologyManager had a hard‑coded limit of 8 NUMA nodes (maxAllowableNUMANodes). On nodes with more than 8 NUMA nodes this caused the manager to abort enumeration of NUMA affinities, preventing pod placement that requires NUMA awareness.
enrichment.affected: Kubelet’s TopologyManager and any workloads that rely on NUMA‑aware pod placement, especially on nodes with more than eight NUMA nodes.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new kubelet TopologyManager policy option `max-allowable-numa-nodes` that lets users configure `maxAllowableNUMANodes` via the kubelet configuration, removing the fixed 8‑node ceiling.
enrichment.impact: Clusters with high‑NUMA nodes can now enable the TopologyManager without hitting the hard limit, improving pod placement flexibility and avoiding failures on large‑scale hardware. Users gain control to raise the limit as needed while a future refactor removes the underlying state‑explosion issue.

feature.description: Kubelet would not restart the container when fields other than image in the Pod spec change. pod spec change.
feature.author: HirazawaUi
feature.userFacingChange: Kubelet will not restart the container when fields other than image in the pod spec change.

issueContext.title: Enabling InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature gate causes restart of containers within the cluster
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

We recently enabled the InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature gate which caused the container spec of our containers to change which in turn triggered container restart logic on the kubelet. All the containers in our cluster we restarted at the same time.

### What did you expect to happen?

Containers shouldn't restart when the InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature gate is enabled

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Enable InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature gate, observe k8s events for pods after restarting apiserver:
```
1h39m  Normal   Killing    Container XXX definition changed, will be restarted
```

### Anything else we need to know?

This issue is caused since enabling the feature gate causes the apiserver to update the container spec with a default policy here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d61cbac69aae97db1839bd2e0e86d68f26b353a7/pkg/apis/core/v1/defaults.go#L181

That causes the logic here to restart the container since the container spec changed: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d61cbac69aae97db1839bd2e0e86d68f26b353a7/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_manager.go#L991

You can also easily verify that the container spec changed using kubectl:
```
# before apiserver restart with InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature gate 
$ kubectl get pod XXX -n NNN -o json | grep resize

# after apiserver restart with InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature gate 
$ kubectl get pod XXX -n NNN -o json | grep resize
                "resizePolicy": [
```

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
v1.27.5
```

</details>


### Cloud provider

<details>

</details>


### OS version

<details>

```console
# On Linux:
$ cat /etc/os-release
# paste output here
$ uname -a
# paste output here

# On Windows:
C:\> wmic os get Caption, Version, BuildNumber, OSArchitecture
# paste output here
```

</details>


### Install tools

<details>

</details>


### Container runtime

enrichment.problem: Kubelet incorrectly restarted containers whenever any field in the pod spec changed (e.g., default fields added by the InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature gate), even when the container image remained the same, causing unnecessary pod restarts.
enrichment.affected: All pods whose specifications are updated with non‑image fields (e.g., after enabling InPlacePodVerticalScaling) experienced unwanted restarts.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now restricts restart logic to changes in the container image field only; updates to other pod spec fields no longer trigger a container restart.
enrichment.impact: Prevents mass, unnecessary restarts of pods when non‑image spec fields are modified, improving stability for workloads using feature gates like InPlacePodVerticalScaling and reducing downtime.

feature.description: The scheduler implemented QueueingHint in the TaintToleration plugin, enhancing the throughput of scheduling.
feature.author: sanposhiho
feature.userFacingChange: The scheduler implements QueueingHint in TaintToleration plugin, which enhances the throughput of scheduling.

enrichment.problem: The scheduler's TaintToleration plugin did not provide a QueueingHint, which limited the efficiency and throughput of the scheduling cycle, especially under high pod churn.
enrichment.affected: All clusters using the default kube-scheduler with the TaintToleration plugin; pods that rely on taints and tolerations for node placement.
enrichment.fix: Implemented QueueingHint support in the TaintToleration plugin, allowing the scheduler to better batch and prioritize pod scheduling decisions and improve overall throughput.
enrichment.impact: Clusters experience higher scheduling throughput and lower latency, benefiting large-scale workloads and reducing scheduling back‑pressure.

feature.description: The name of CEL(Common Expression Language) optional type has been changed from `optional` to `optional_type`.
feature.author: jiahuif
feature.userFacingChange: The name of CEL optional type has been changed from `optional` to `optional_type`.

enrichment.problem: The CEL (Common Expression Language) optional type was named `optional`, which conflicted with existing keywords and could cause confusion for users writing CEL expressions in Kubernetes APIs.
enrichment.affected: Developers and operators who use CEL expressions in Kubernetes resources (e.g., admission controllers, validation rules) will need to update their expressions and related code.
enrichment.fix: Rename the CEL optional type from `optional` to `optional_type` throughout the codebase, API definitions, and documentation.
enrichment.impact: Improves clarity and prevents naming conflicts when authoring CEL expressions, but requires users and developers to update any references to the old type name.

feature.description: Added support for CEL(Common Expression Language) expressions and `additionalProperties` to be used under nested quantifiers in CRD schemas.
feature.author: alexzielenski
feature.userFacingChange: CEL expressions and `additionalProperties` are now allowed to be used under nested quantifiers in CRD schemas

enrichment.problem: CRD schemas did not allow CEL expressions or additionalProperties to be used inside nested quantifiers (e.g., arrays of objects), limiting validation capabilities for complex custom resources.
enrichment.affected: Developers creating or maintaining CustomResourceDefinitions that include nested arrays or maps and want to leverage CEL or additionalProperties for validation.
enrichment.fix: Extended the CRD schema validation engine to permit CEL expressions and the additionalProperties keyword under nested quantifier constructs, enabling richer validation rules in complex schemas.
enrichment.impact: CRD authors can now write more expressive and precise validation logic for complex resource structures, reducing the need for external admission controllers and improving reliability of custom resources.

feature.description: kube-proxy's nftables mode (--proxy-mode=nftables) is now beta and available by default.
feature.author: danwinship
feature.userFacingChange:
kube-proxy's nftables mode is now beta and available by default. It
requires Linux kernel version 5.13 or later, and can be enabled by
passing `--proxy-mode=nftables` to kube-proxy.

A few features in the nftables mode behave slightly differently than
in the iptables mode:

  - By default, nftables mode only listens for NodePort connections on
    the node's primary interface, and it never listens for NodePort
    connections on 127.0.0.1.

  - If you are running a firewall on the node, nftables kube-proxy
    requires the firewall to be configured properly for service
    proxying; it will not try to poke holes in the firewall itself.

  - The nftables mode does not attempt to work around conntrack bugs
    in the kernel unless you explicitly configure it to.

Consult the documentation
(https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/networking/virtual-ips/#proxy-mode-nftables)
for more information on how to tell if these differences affect you,
and what configuration options are available to change these behaviors.

Note that while the nftables code should be stable and fully-featured
at this point, it is still in the process of being optimized, and it
is known to have worse performance than iptables mode in a few
situations. (In particular, kube-proxy startup for a given cluster
size will be slower with nftables mode than with iptables mode.)

enrichment.problem: kube-proxy lacked a stable, default nftables implementation, forcing users to rely on iptables mode which may not be optimal for future Linux kernels and certain networking setups.
enrichment.affected: All clusters using kube-proxy, especially those running NodePort services or custom firewalls, and only on nodes with Linux kernel 5.13 or newer.
enrichment.fix: Introduced nftables mode for kube-proxy as a beta feature that is enabled by default on supported clusters. Users can explicitly select it with `--proxy-mode=nftables`. Documentation details behavioral differences, kernel version requirements (>=5.13), firewall configuration needs, and optional conntrack settings.
enrichment.impact: Provides a path forward to replace iptables with nftables, aligning with modern Linux kernel networking. Clusters on kernel 5.13+ can use the new mode, but must verify firewall rules and accept potential slower kube-proxy startup and slightly lower performance in some cases. Improves long‑term maintainability and feature completeness of kube-proxy.

feature.description:
'kubeadm: marked the flag "--experimental-output'' as deprecated (it will
be removed in a future release) and added a new flag ''--output" that serves the
same purpose. Affected commands are - "kubeadm config images list", "kubeadm token
list", "kubeadm upgrade plan", "kubeadm certs check-expiration".'
feature.author: carlory
feature.userFacingChange: kubeadm: mark the flag "--experimental-output' as deprecated (it will be removed in a future release) and add a new flag '--output" that serves the same purpose. Affected commands are - "kubeadm config images list", "kubeadm token list", "kubeadm upgade plan", "kubeadm certs check-expiration".

enrichment.problem: The kubeadm CLI flag "--experimental-output" was undocumented as deprecated, leading to potential usage of a flag that will be removed in future releases.
enrichment.affected: Any user or automation that runs kubeadm commands (config images list, token list, upgrade plan, certs check-expiration) with the "--experimental-output" flag.
enrichment.fix: The flag "--experimental-output" is now marked deprecated and a new stable flag "--output" is added that provides the same functionality. Existing commands continue to work with the old flag but will emit a deprecation warning.
enrichment.impact: Users and automation scripts that rely on "--experimental-output" must switch to "--output" to avoid future breakage. This change clarifies the supported flag and prepares for removal of the experimental flag.

feature.description: kubeadm: Used output/v1alpha3 to print structural output for the commands "kubeadm config images list" and "kubeadm token list".
feature.author: carlory
feature.userFacingChange: kubeadm: use output/v1alpha3 to print structural output for the commands "kubeadm config images list" and "kubeadm token list".

enrichment.problem: The `kubeadm config images list` and `kubeadm token list` commands emitted unstructured, human‑readable text, making it difficult for scripts and automation tools to parse their output reliably.
enrichment.affected: Users running `kubeadm config images list` or `kubeadm token list`, especially those automating cluster bootstrapping or upgrades.
enrichment.fix: Both commands now use the `output/v1alpha3` format, providing structured (JSON/YAML) output that can be programmatically consumed.
enrichment.impact: Automation, CI/CD pipelines, and tooling that rely on machine‑readable data from kubeadm can now parse command results directly without fragile text processing, improving reliability and integration consistency.

feature.description: kubeadm: Switched to using the new etcd endpoints introduced in 3.5.11 - /livez (for liveness probe) and /readyz (for readyness and startup probe). With this change it is no longer possible to deploy a custom etcd version older than 3.5.11 with kubeadm 1.31. If so, please upgrade etcd to a supported version.
feature.author: neolit123
feature.userFacingChange: kubeadm: switch to using the new etcd endpoints introduced in 3.5.11 - /livez (for liveness probe) and /readyz (for readyness and startup probe). With this change it is no longer possible to deploy a custom etcd version older than 3.5.11 with kubeadm 1.31. If so, please upgrade.

enrichment.problem: kubeadm 1.31 switched to the new etcd health endpoints (/livez and /readyz) that were added in etcd 3.5.11. Custom deployments using an etcd version older than 3.5.11 do not expose these endpoints, causing kubeadm’s liveness, readiness, and startup probes to fail.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that were using a custom etcd version older than 3.5.11 with kubeadm 1.31. The change affects the kubeadm initialization/upgrade process and the etcd component's health probes.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now uses the /livez and /readyz endpoints for health checking. Users must run etcd version 3.5.11 or newer (or upgrade their custom etcd) for kubeadm to function correctly.
enrichment.impact: Ensures more reliable health checking for etcd, but breaks clusters that were running custom etcd versions older than 3.5.11. Those clusters must upgrade etcd before initializing or upgrading with kubeadm 1.31.

feature.description:
Introduces new functionality to the client-go's `List` method, allowing users to enable API streaming. To activate this feature, users can set the `client-go.WatchListClient` feature gate.

It is important to note that the server must support streaming for this feature to function properly. If streaming is not supported by the server, client-go will revert to using the normal `LIST` method to obtain data.
feature.author: p0lyn0mial
feature.userFacingChange:
Introduces new functionality to the client-go's `List` method, allowing users to enable API streaming. To activate this feature, users can set the `client-go.WatchListClient` feature gate.

It is important to note that the server must support streaming for this feature to function properly. If streaming is not supported by the server, client-go will revert to using the normal `LIST` method to obtain data.

enrichment.problem: The List method in client-go could not stream results, requiring full list retrieval even for large datasets, limiting efficiency and latency for consumers.
enrichment.affected: Applications and controllers that use client-go's List API. They can opt‑in to streaming for more efficient data retrieval.
enrichment.fix: Adds optional streaming support to client-go's List method behind the client-go.WatchListClient feature gate. When enabled and the server supports streaming, List will receive data via a stream; otherwise it falls back to the traditional LIST call.
enrichment.impact: Clients can receive list data incrementally, reducing memory pressure and latency for large result sets. No breaking change; existing behavior remains when the feature is disabled or the server lacks streaming support.

feature.description: Added the ability to the kubelet server to dynamically load certificate files.
feature.author: zhangweikop
feature.userFacingChange: kubelet server can now dynamically load certificate files

enrichment.problem: Kubelet required static TLS certificate files that were only read at startup, so rotating certificates required restarting the kubelet, causing downtime and operational friction.
enrichment.affected: All clusters that run kubelet with TLS certificates that may need rotation, especially those using automated certificate management solutions.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet server now watches the configured certificate and key files and reloads them automatically when they change, allowing dynamic certificate rotation without a restart.
enrichment.impact: Administrators can rotate kubelet TLS certificates (e.g., for expiration or compromise) without disrupting node operation, improving security posture and availability of workloads.

feature.description: Added completion for `kubectl set image`.
feature.author: ah8ad3
feature.userFacingChange: Adds completion for `kubectl set image`.

enrichment.problem: kubectl did not provide shell auto-completion for the `set image` command, requiring users to remember the exact syntax and flags.
enrichment.affected: All users of kubectl who use shell completion (bash, zsh, fish, etc.) when running `kubectl set image`.
enrichment.fix: Adds shell completion support for `kubectl set image`, enabling tab‑completion of subcommand arguments and flags.
enrichment.impact: Makes the CLI easier to use and reduces errors for developers and operators who rely on bash/zsh/fish completions when updating container images via kubectl.

feature.description: Added check for etcd version to warn about deprecated etcd versions if `ConsistentListFromCache` is enabled.
feature.author: ah8ad3
feature.userFacingChange: Checking etcd version to warn about deprecated etcd versions if `ConsistentListFromCache` is enabled.

issueContext.title: Implement checking etcd version to warn about deprecated etcd versions
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Part of https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/2340

From https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/2340-Consistent-reads-from-cache/README.md#bug-in-etcd-progress-notification

> Only recently community discovered a bug https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/issues/15220 for requesting progress notification. This bug causes a race between sending an event and progress notification with the same revision. Normally we would expect to event to always come first, however due to the bug, progress notification might be sent first. Serving a consistent lists in that situation could result in returning too early and missing the event. The bug was only fixed in v3.4.25 and v3.5.8 (both 9 months old), which is too fresh for Kubernetes to not handle.
> 
> Our tests have shown that with the bug manual progress notification cannot be trusted at all. It causes a silent corruption that cannot be automatically detected prior to acting upon the corrupted data. For Beta, we propose to conditionally enable the feature in a way that mitigates the risk of unaware users stumbling on the bug.
> 
> We propose to implement a safeguard that will prevent enabling ConsistentListFromCache on etcd version with broken progress notification. During kube-apiserver startup we will verify etcd version by calling Status method and checking etcd patch version. The condition will only pass if all etcd endpoints have etcd version that includes the fix for https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/issues/15220.
> 
> The proposed behavior of the safeguard for Beta:
> 
> etcd version could not be acquired or etcd new enough - warn, but continue with whatever the current value of the feature gate is
> * etcd too old, feature gate not explicitly specified - warn and disable the feature
> * etcd too old, feature gate explicitly enabled - abort
> * etcd new enough - use whatever the current value of the feature gate is
>
> T

enrichment.problem: When ConsistentListFromCache is enabled, clusters using older etcd versions (pre v3.4.25 or v3.5.8) encounter a bug in etcd's progress notification that can cause a race, leading to premature list termination and silent data corruption.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that enable ConsistentListFromCache while running etcd versions older than v3.4.25/v3.5.8 would experience silent corruption of list results.
enrichment.fix: The kube-apiserver now checks the etcd version during startup (via the Status call). If any etcd endpoint is running a version with the known bug, it emits a warning and prevents enabling ConsistentListFromCache on that cluster.
enrichment.impact: Administrators are alerted before enabling the feature on unsupported etcd versions, avoiding potential data inconsistency and loss. It ensures the ConsistentListFromCache feature is only used with etcd releases that have the bug fixed.

feature.description: client-go/reflector: warns when the bookmark event for initial events hasn't been received
feature.author: p0lyn0mial

enrichment.problem: Reflector in client-go could start watching a resource without receiving an initial bookmark event, and it produced no indication that this critical synchronization step was missed.
enrichment.affected: Any controller, operator, or custom program that uses client-go informers or watches with bookmark support.
enrichment.fix: Added a warning log when the initial set of events is received without a preceding bookmark event, making the situation visible to developers and operators.
enrichment.impact: Improves observability for controllers and other components that rely on client-go watches, helping detect misbehaving API servers or network issues earlier.

feature.description: Improved memory usage of kube-apiserver by dropping`.metadata.managedFields` field that self-requested informers of kube-apiserver didn't need.
feature.author: linxiulei
feature.userFacingChange: Improve memory usage of kube-apiserver by dropping the `.metadata.managedFields` field that self-requested informers of kube-apiserver doesn't need.

enrichment.problem: kube-apiserver’s self‑requested informers stored the entire `.metadata.managedFields` field for each object, which is unnecessary and caused higher than needed memory consumption.
enrichment.affected: All clusters running kube-apiserver; the memory usage of the apiserver component is reduced.
enrichment.fix: The apiserver now drops the `.metadata.managedFields` field when populating self‑requested informers, eliminating the redundant data storage.
enrichment.impact: Reduces the memory footprint of kube-apiserver, improving scalability and lowering resource requirements for control‑plane nodes, especially in large clusters.

feature.description:
Promoted `generateName` retries to beta, and made the `NameGenerationRetries` feature gate
enabled by default.
You can read https://kep.k8s.io/4420 for more details.
feature.author: jpbetz
feature.userFacingChange:
Promoted `generateName` retries to beta, and made the `NameGenerationRetries` feature gate
enabled by default.
You can read https://kep.k8s.io/4420 for more details.

enrichment.problem: Objects created with a generateName field could collide with existing names, and the API server would only try once, causing creation failures. The NameGenerationRetries feature gate existed to allow additional attempts, but it was off by default, so users did not benefit from the retry logic.
enrichment.affected: All clusters that create resources using the generateName field, especially in high‑throughput or multi‑tenant environments where name collisions are more likely.
enrichment.fix: The generateName retry logic has been promoted to beta and the NameGenerationRetries feature gate is now enabled by default. The API server will now automatically retry name generation a few times before giving up, reducing collision‑related failures.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability for any workload that relies on generateName (e.g., Pods, Jobs, Deployments, StatefulSets). Users see fewer creation errors due to name collisions without needing to enable a feature gate manually.

feature.description: Added Custom resource field selectors in beta and enabled them by default. Check out https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4358 for more details.
feature.author: jpbetz
feature.userFacingChange: Custom resource field selectors are now in beta and enabled by default. Check out https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4358 for more details.

enrichment.problem: Custom resources could not be filtered using field selectors, limiting clients (e.g., kubectl, controllers) from efficiently listing or watching specific CR instances based on field values.
enrichment.affected: Any workload or tool that interacts with custom resources and needs server‑side filtering (e.g., operators, kubectl, custom controllers).
enrichment.fix: Implemented support for field selectors on custom resources, promoted to beta and enabled by default. The API server now parses and matches field selectors for CRDs just like built‑in resources.
enrichment.impact: Users can now perform server‑side filtering on CRs, reducing client‑side processing and bandwidth, simplifying controller and CLI implementations that need to target specific CR objects.

feature.description: Added ports autocompletion for kubectl port-foward command.
feature.author: TessaIO

enrichment.problem: kubectl port-forward did not provide autocompletion for the ports argument, requiring users to remember or look up port numbers manually.
enrichment.affected: Anyone using the kubectl port-forward command, particularly when working in interactive shells that support completion.
enrichment.fix: Implemented shell autocompletion support for the ports flag in the kubectl port-forward command, enabling tab-completion of valid port numbers.
enrichment.impact: Improves developer productivity and reduces errors when using kubectl port-forward, especially in interactive shells.

feature.description:
kubeadm: Switched kubeadm to start using the CRI client library instead of shelling out of the `crictl` binary
for actions against a CRI endpoint. The kubeadm deb/rpm packages will continue to install the `cri-tools`
package for one more release, but in you must adapt your scripts to install `crictl` manually from
https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cri-tools/releases or a different location.

The `kubeadm` package will stop depending on the `cri-tools` package in Kubernetes 1.32, which means that
installing `kubeadm` will no longer automatically ensure installation of `crictl`.
feature.author: saschagrunert
feature.userFacingChange:
kubeadm: switched kubeadm to start using the CRI client library instead of shelling out of the `crictl` binary
for actions against a CRI endpoint. The kubeadm deb/rpm packages will continue to install the `cri-tools`
package for one more release, but in you must adapt your scripts to install `crictl` manually from
https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cri-tools/releases or a different location.

The `kubeadm` package will stop depending on the `cri-tools` package in Kubernetes 1.32, which means that
installing `kubeadm` will no longer automatically ensure installation of `crictl`.

enrichment.problem: The kubeadm packages previously depended on the cri-tools package, which automatically installed the `crictl` binary. kubeadm now uses the CRI client library directly and will stop depending on cri-tools in v1.32, so scripts that assume `crictl` is installed with kubeadm will fail.
enrichment.affected: Any environment that installs kubeadm via the Debian or RPM packages and expects the `crictl` binary to be present automatically, as well as automation scripts that invoke `crictl` assuming it was installed by kubeadm.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm has been updated to use the internal CRI client library instead of invoking the `crictl` binary. Starting with the next release, the kubeadm deb/rpm packages will no longer pull in cri-tools; users must manually install `crictl` (e.g., from the cri-tools releases page) if they need it.
enrichment.impact: Installing kubeadm will no longer guarantee that `crictl` is present. Users and automation that rely on the binary being available must adjust their provisioning scripts to install it separately. kubeadm functionality itself is unaffected because it now uses the library directly.

feature.description: kubeadm: Ensured that during "upgrade" , if the "etcd.yaml" static pod did not need upgrade, still consider rotating the etcd certificates and restarting the etcd static pod if the "kube-apiserver.yaml" manifest was to be upgraded and if certificate renewal was not disabled.
feature.author: neolit123
feature.userFacingChange: kubeadm: during "upgrade" , if the "etcd.yaml" static pod does not need upgrade, still consider rotating the etcd certificates and restarting the etcd static pod if the "kube-apiserver.yaml" manifest is to be upgraded and if certificate renewal is not disabled.

enrichment.problem: During a kubeadm upgrade, if the etcd static pod (etcd.yaml) did not need an upgrade, kubeadm would skip rotating etcd TLS certificates and restarting the etcd pod even when the kube-apiserver static pod (kube-apiserver.yaml) was being upgraded. This could leave the API server with mismatched certificates, causing communication failures between the API server and etcd.
enrichment.affected: Clusters upgraded with kubeadm where the etcd static pod is already at the target version but the kube-apiserver manifest is upgraded and certificate renewal is enabled.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now always evaluates etcd certificate renewal and restarts the etcd static pod when the kube-apiserver manifest is scheduled for upgrade, regardless of whether the etcd static pod itself requires a version upgrade, unless certificate renewal is explicitly disabled.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that the control‑plane remains functional during upgrades by preventing certificate mismatches, reducing the risk of API server outages or loss of etcd connectivity when upgrading the API server.

feature.description: Added flag to `kubectl logs` called `--all-pods` to get all pods from a object that uses a pod selector.
feature.author: cmwylie19

enrichment.problem: kubectl logs could only retrieve logs from a single pod; users had no simple way to get logs from all pods selected by an object's pod selector (e.g., all pods of a Deployment or DaemonSet).
enrichment.affected: Anyone using `kubectl logs` to view logs of workloads that manage multiple pods (Deployments, DaemonSets, StatefulSets, etc.).
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new `--all-pods` flag to `kubectl logs` that automatically streams logs from every pod matching the selector of the specified higher‑level object.
enrichment.impact: Makes it easier and faster for developers and operators to debug multi‑pod workloads, reducing the need for manual looping or scripting to collect logs from each pod.

feature.description: Scheduler changes its logic of calculating `evaluatedNodes` from "contains the number of nodes that filtered out by PreFilterResult and Filter plugins" to "the number of nodes filtered out by Filter plugins only".
feature.author: AxeZhan

issueContext.title: Change EvaluatedNodes to count Nodes that reach Filter phase only
issueContext.body:
Currently, `EvaluatedNodes` contains the number of nodes that filtered out by PreFilterResult and Filter plugins.
But, before #119779, actually it only contains Nodes reach Filter plugins, which is actually more useful than the current state.

This issue aims to bring back the previous `EvaluatedNodes`.

ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119779#discussion_r1589213337
/cc @alculquicondor 
/sig scheduling
/kind feature

enrichment.problem: The `EvaluatedNodes` metric counted nodes filtered out by both PreFilterResult and Filter plugins, which diverged from its original behavior and could mislead users interpreting scheduler evaluation data.
enrichment.affected: Users and tools that consume the scheduler's `EvaluatedNodes` metric, such as monitoring dashboards and autoscaling components.
enrichment.fix: Scheduler logic for `EvaluatedNodes` was updated to count only nodes that reach the Filter phase (i.e., filtered out by Filter plugins), restoring the original metric semantics.
enrichment.impact: Provides accurate scheduler metrics, improving monitoring, debugging, and any components (e.g., cluster autoscaler) that rely on `EvaluatedNodes` for decision‑making.

feature.description: Updated the CEL default compatibility environment version to 1.30, ensuring that extended libraries added before version 1.30 are available for use.
feature.author: cici37
feature.userFacingChange: CEL default compatibility environment version to updated to 1.30 so that the extended libraries added before 1.30 is available to use.

enrichment.problem: The default CEL compatibility environment version was older than 1.30, so extended CEL libraries added before version 1.30 were not automatically available to users writing CEL expressions for validation, admission, etc.
enrichment.affected: Developers and cluster operators who author CEL expressions for API validation, admission control, or other server‑side expressions.
enrichment.fix: Update the default CEL compatibility environment version to 1.30, making all extended libraries introduced prior to 1.30 available without any additional configuration.
enrichment.impact: Users can now use the full set of pre‑1.30 CEL extensions out‑of‑the‑box, reducing configuration friction and preventing validation failures caused by missing libraries.

feature.description:
'kubeadm: enhanced the "patches" functionality to be able to patch coredns
deployment. The new patch target is called "corednsdeployment" (e.g. patch file
"corednsdeployment+json.json"). This makes it possible to apply custom patches
to coredns deployment during "init" and "upgrade".'
feature.author: SataQiu
feature.userFacingChange: kubeadm: enhance the "patches" functionality to be able to patch coredns deployment. The new patch target is called "corednsdeployment" (e.g. patch file "corednsdeployment+json.json"). This makes it possible to apply custom patches to coredns deployment during "init" and "upgrade".

enrichment.problem: kubeadm could not apply custom patches to the CoreDNS deployment during cluster initialization or upgrade, limiting operators from customizing CoreDNS settings such as replicas, resources, or command‑line flags.
enrichment.affected: Operators who need custom CoreDNS configurations during cluster bootstrapping or upgrades.
enrichment.fix: Added a new patch target named "corednsdeployment" (e.g., a patch file named "corednsdeployment+json.json") to the kubeadm patches functionality, enabling JSON patches to be applied to the CoreDNS Deployment during "kubeadm init" and "kubeadm upgrade".
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators can now tailor CoreDNS deployment parameters without manually editing manifests after bootstrap, streamlining custom configurations and reducing post‑bootstrap manual steps.

feature.description: Built Kubernetes with Go 1.22.3.
feature.author: cpanato
feature.userFacingChange: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.3

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, lacking recent compiler bug fixes, security patches, and performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes binaries (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) built from source are affected by the new Go version.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to compile all Kubernetes components with Go 1.22.3.
enrichment.impact: Clusters benefit from the latest Go runtime security and performance enhancements, and the codebase stays compatible with upcoming Go releases, reducing future upgrade friction.

feature.description: Promote HonorPVReclaimPolicy to beta and enable the feature-gate by default
feature.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: The HonorPVReclaimPolicy feature, which lets PersistentVolume reclaim behavior honor the policy set on the PV, was only available as an alpha feature and disabled by default, preventing users from using it in production.
enrichment.affected: Users of PersistentVolumes and PersistentVolumeClaims who need the PV reclaim policy to be respected, especially those running stateful workloads on storage backends.
enrichment.fix: Promoted the HonorPVReclaimPolicy feature to beta and enabled its feature gate by default, making the functionality generally available without manual gating.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now reliably use the HonorPVReclaimPolicy to control PV lifecycle, improving storage management and reducing unexpected volume deletions for workloads that depend on specific reclaim policies.

feature.description: Added a feature to report an event about a Pod if kubelet observes a failed attach operation, even if the kubelet is running with `--enable-controller-attach-detach=false`.
feature.author: carlory
feature.userFacingChange: report an event to pod if kubelet does attach operation failed when kubelet is running with `--enable-controller-attach-detach=false`

enrichment.problem: When the kubelet is started with --enable-controller-attach-detach=false, failed volume attach operations did not generate any event on the associated Pod, making it difficult for users to diagnose attach failures.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running kubelet with --enable-controller-attach-detach=false, especially those using CSI drivers or other volume plugins that may experience attach failures.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now reports a Kubernetes event on the corresponding Pod whenever it observes a failed attach operation, even when controller attach/detach is disabled.
enrichment.impact: Users gain immediate visibility into volume attach failures through standard Pod events, improving troubleshooting and reducing time to resolve storage issues in clusters that disable controller attach/detach.

feature.description: Users can traverse all the pods that are in the scheduler and waiting in the permit stage through method `IterateOverWaitingPods`. In other words,  all waitingPods in scheduler can be obtained from any profiles. Before this commit, each profile could only obtain waitingPods within that profile.
feature.author: kerthcet

issueContext.title: Scheduler:  Share `frameworkImpl.waitingPods` among profiles
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

I hope to share the `waitingPods` among multiple profiles, instead of creating a new `waitingPods` in each profiles with the current implementation.

In other words, `waitingPods` is only instantiated once in a scheduler app.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a1ffdedf782edf1472102b0b99c1467d4ed39753/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L253-L258


@Huang-Wei @ahg-g  PTAL, Is there any negative impact of this change that I didn't consider, thanks.

### Why is this needed?

In some scenarios, I need to traverse `all pods` waiting in the permit stage within the current scheduler app, rather than the pods that using the current profile for scheduling and waiting in the permit stage.

For example, we want use [coscheduling](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/scheduler-plugins/blob/master/pkg/coscheduling/README.md) to achieve `all-or-nothing`. And we have abstracted the concept of a `Cluster`, where there are two deployments under each cluster. Each deployments use different scheduler profile, and one cluster corresponds to one podGroup, as following:
![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/18323315/256ffd20-6adc-4dc5-b249-d6ffcafed303)

Then, we want pods in one cluster (podA1, podA2, podB1) to be scheduled succeed/failed together. 

We assume that all pods can pass through the filter plugins, and `podA2` is the last to be scheduled. At this point, `podA1` and `podB1` are both waiting in the permit stage. Afterwards, we traverse the `waitingPods` to complete the permit waiting for `podA1` and `podB1`. However, from an implementation perspective, now we can only see `podA1` in `waitingPods`, `podB1` cannot be seen, because`podA2` & `podB1` use different scheduling profiles. Which will cause `podB1` timeout during the permit phase, even if all pods within the podGroup are successfully scheduled.

enrichment.problem: Each scheduler profile maintained its own waitingPods list, so plugins could only see pods waiting in the permit stage for that specific profile. This prevented traversing or coordinating all waiting pods across multiple profiles.
enrichment.affected: Users running multiple scheduler profiles, especially those using plugins that need to see all waiting pods (e.g., coscheduling), and the scheduler itself.
enrichment.fix: The waitingPods structure is now shared across all scheduler profiles. A new method `IterateOverWaitingPods` allows enumeration of every pod in the permit stage regardless of which profile it belongs to.
enrichment.impact: Plugins and custom schedulers (e.g., coscheduling) can now coordinate pods across profiles for all‑or‑nothing scheduling or other cross‑profile logic, simplifying implementation and improving correctness for multi‑profile clusters.

feature.description: The sidecars' finish time will now be accounted for when calculating the job's finish time.
feature.author: AxeZhan
feature.userFacingChange: The sidecar finish time will be accounted when calculating the job's finish time.

issueContext.title: [Sidecar Containers] Sidecar containers finish time needs to be accounted for in job controller
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Today the function `getFinishTimeFromContainers` (pkg/controller/job/backoff_utils.go) only account for the regular containers finish time,
presumably assuming that init containers have completed before before.
However, with the sidecar (restartable init) containers, sidecar containers will always finish later than
regular containers. And those needs to be accounted for the calculation.

/kind bug

### What did you expect to happen?

The sidecar finish time will be accounted when calculating the job's finish time.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Sidecar container with prolonged termination logic on a job will result in incorrect finish time reporting.

### Anything else we need to know?

/sig apps
/priority backlog
KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/753

enrichment.problem: Job controller only considered main containers when calculating a Job's finish time, ignoring sidecar (restartable init) containers that may finish later, leading to inaccurate Job completion timestamps.
enrichment.affected: Jobs that run sidecar containers (restartable init containers). Their reported completion time was earlier than the actual termination of the sidecar.
enrichment.fix: The Job controller now includes sidecar container termination times in the computation of the Job's overall finish time.
enrichment.impact: Job finish timestamps become accurate for workloads that use sidecar containers, improving observability, cleanup logic, and any downstream processes that rely on correct Job completion times.

feature.description:
The kube-scheduler added support for scheduling hints for the StorageClass resource within the VolumeBinding plugin.
The scheduling hints allowed the scheduler to retry scheduling a Pod that was previously rejected by the VolumeBinding plugin only if a new resource referenced by the plugin was created or an existing resource referenced by the plugin was updated.
feature.author: bells17
feature.userFacingChange:
kube-scheduler implements scheduling hints for the VolumeBinding plugin.
The scheduling hints allow the scheduler to retry scheduling a Pod that was previously rejected by the VolumeBinding plugin only if a new resource referenced by the plugin was created or an existing resource referenced by the plugin was updated.

enrichment.problem: When a Pod was rejected by the VolumeBinding plugin because required PersistentVolume resources were not yet created or bound, the scheduler would not retry scheduling the Pod after those resources became available, leaving the Pod stuck in Pending.
enrichment.affected: Pods using PersistentVolumeClaims that go through the VolumeBinding plugin (e.g., StatefulSets, Deployments) were affected because they could remain pending indefinitely after an initial binding failure.
enrichment.fix: kube-scheduler now supports scheduling hints for the VolumeBinding plugin. The scheduler will automatically retry scheduling a previously rejected Pod when a new resource referenced by the plugin is created or an existing referenced resource is updated (e.g., a PVC becomes bound).
enrichment.impact: Pods that depend on dynamic storage provisioning or delayed volume binding can now become scheduled automatically once the storage resources are ready, reducing manual intervention and improving pod startup reliability.

feature.description:
The kube-scheduler added support for scheduling hints for the PersistentVolumeClaim resource within the VolumeBinding plugin.
The scheduling hints allowed the scheduler to retry scheduling a Pod that was previously rejected by the VolumeBinding plugin only if a new resource referenced by the plugin was created or an existing resource referenced by the plugin was updated.
feature.author: bells17
feature.userFacingChange:
kube-scheduler implements scheduling hints for the VolumeBinding plugin.
The scheduling hints allow the scheduler to retry scheduling a Pod that was previously rejected by the VolumeBinding plugin only if a new resource referenced by the plugin was created or an existing resource referenced by the plugin was updated.

enrichment.problem: Pods with PersistentVolumeClaims could be rejected by the VolumeBinding plugin and would not be automatically retried when the required PVC became available, causing scheduling delays and requiring manual intervention.
enrichment.affected: Pods that reference PersistentVolumeClaims and were previously rejected by the VolumeBinding plugin; cluster operators managing such workloads.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now implements scheduling hints for the VolumeBinding plugin. When a new PVC is created or an existing PVC referenced by the plugin is updated, the scheduler receives a hint and retries scheduling the previously rejected pod.
enrichment.impact: Pods that depend on PVCs are scheduled more promptly once the volume resources are ready, reducing manual remediation and improving overall workload availability.

feature.description:
The kube-scheduler added support for scheduling hints for the CSIStorageCapacity resource within the VolumeBinding plugin.
The scheduling hints allowed the scheduler to retry scheduling a Pod that was previously rejected by the VolumeBinding plugin only if a new resource referenced by the plugin was created or an existing resource referenced by the plugin was updated.
feature.author: bells17
feature.userFacingChange:
kube-scheduler implements scheduling hints for the VolumeBinding plugin.
The scheduling hints allow the scheduler to retry scheduling a Pod that was previously rejected by the VolumeBinding plugin only if a new resource referenced by the plugin was created or an existing resource referenced by the plugin was updated.

enrichment.problem: When a pod was rejected by the VolumeBinding plugin because the required CSIStorageCapacity was not available, the scheduler did not retry the pod even after a suitable CSIStorageCapacity object was created or updated, causing the pod to remain unschedulable.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using CSI drivers with volume binding mode; pods that were previously stuck in Pending due to missing CSIStorageCapacity.
enrichment.fix: kube-scheduler now implements scheduling hints for the VolumeBinding plugin. The scheduler watches CSIStorageCapacity resources referenced by the plugin and will retry scheduling the previously rejected pod only when a new relevant resource is created or an existing one is updated.
enrichment.impact: Pods that depend on dynamic storage provisioning (e.g., PVCs with WaitForFirstConsumer) can now be scheduled promptly after storage capacity becomes available, reducing scheduling delays and improving workload availability.

feature.description: Added namespace autocompletion for `kubectl config set-context` command.
feature.author: TessaIO
feature.userFacingChange: Added namespace autocompletion for kubectl config set-context command

enrichment.problem: kubectl config set-context did not provide tab-completion for the --namespace flag, requiring users to type full namespace names manually.
enrichment.affected: CLI users who configure contexts with `kubectl config set-context`, especially those working with many namespaces.
enrichment.fix: Implemented shell autocompletion for the namespace argument of the `kubectl config set-context` command.
enrichment.impact: Improves developer productivity and reduces typing errors when switching contexts, making the CLI more user‑friendly.

feature.description:
kube-scheduler implements scheduling hints for the VolumeZone plugin.
The scheduling hints allow the scheduler to only retry scheduling a Pod
that was previously rejected by the VolemeZone plugin if  addition/update of node, 
addition/update of PV, addition/update of PVC, or addition of SC matches pod's topology settings.
feature.author: Gekko0114
feature.userFacingChange:
kube-scheduler implements scheduling hints for the VolumeZone plugin.
The scheduling hints allow the scheduler to only retry scheduling a Pod
that was previously rejected by the VolemeZone plugin if  addition/update of node, 
addition/update of PV, addition/update of PVC, or addition of SC matches pod's topology settings.

enrichment.problem: The VolumeZone plugin could cause the scheduler to repeatedly retry scheduling a Pod that was previously rejected due to topology constraints, even when unrelated node or volume changes occurred, leading to wasted scheduler cycles and delayed pod placement.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the VolumeZone plugin (typically CSI drivers with topology) and Pods that have volume topology requirements.
enrichment.fix: Implemented scheduling hints for the VolumeZone plugin. The scheduler now only retries a Pod if the addition or update of a node, PersistentVolume, PersistentVolumeClaim, or StorageClass aligns with the Pod's topology settings, preventing unnecessary retries.
enrichment.impact: Reduces unnecessary scheduler work and improves scheduling latency for workloads that depend on volume topology constraints, leading to more efficient use of cluster resources.

feature.description:
kube-scheduler implements scheduling hints for the VolumeZone plugin.
The scheduling hints allow the scheduler to only retry scheduling a Pod
that was previously rejected by the VolemeZone plugin if  addition/update of node, 
addition/update of PV, addition/update of PVC, or addition of SC matches pod's topology settings.
feature.author: Gekko0114

kube-scheduler implements scheduling hints for the VolumeZone plugin.
The scheduling hints allow the scheduler to only retry scheduling a Pod
that was previously rejected by the VolemeZone plugin if  addition/update of node,

enrichment.problem: When a Pod is rejected by the VolumeZone plugin due to topology constraints, the scheduler would keep retrying the Pod even if no relevant topology‑related changes occurred, causing unnecessary scheduling cycles and API‑server load.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use PersistentVolumes with topology constraints (e.g., zone‑aware storage) were repeatedly retried by the scheduler even when the cluster state hadn't changed in a way that could satisfy those constraints.
enrichment.fix: kube‑scheduler now receives scheduling hints from the VolumeZone plugin. The scheduler will only retry a previously rejected Pod when a node, PersistentVolume, PersistentVolumeClaim, or StorageClass is added or updated in a way that matches the Pod's topology settings.
enrichment.impact: Reduces wasted scheduling attempts, lowering control‑plane load and speeding up pod placement for workloads that depend on volume topology constraints. Users see faster scheduling when relevant changes happen and fewer noisy rescheduling loops otherwise.

that was previously rejected by the VolemeZone plugin if  addition/update of node,

enrichment.problem: When the VolumeZone plugin rejected a Pod because of topology constraints, kube-scheduler would retry scheduling the Pod even if no relevant topology changes occurred, leading to wasted scheduling cycles.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use PersistentVolumes with topology constraints and were previously rejected by the VolumeZone plugin.
enrichment.fix: Adds scheduling hints to the VolumeZone plugin. The scheduler now only retries a previously rejected Pod if a node, PersistentVolume, PersistentVolumeClaim, or StorageClass is added/updated and now matches the Pod's topology requirements.
