enrichment.fix: The change updates the allowed emulation version range (or bumps the maximum) in the apiserver’s feature‑gate validation logic so that version 1.32 is accepted, aligning the check with the current release’s feature‑gate set.
enrichment.impact: Developers can now build and run the sample-apiserver (and other custom API servers) against current Kubernetes clusters without manual version pinning, restoring CI pipelines and simplifying testing of API extensions.

bugOrRegression.description: Added `/sys/devices/virtual/powercap` to default masked paths. It avoids the potential security risk that the ability to read these files may offer a power-based sidechannel attack against any workloads running on the same kernel.
bugOrRegression.author: carlory
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: Add `/sys/devices/virtual/powercap` to default masked paths. It avoids the potential security risk that the ability to read these files may offer a power-based sidechannel attack against any workloads running on the same kernel.

enrichment.problem: Containers could read /sys/devices/virtual/powercap, exposing power consumption data that could be used for a side‑channel attack against other workloads sharing the same kernel.
enrichment.affected: Any pod/container running on a node could have been used to infer power metrics of co‑located workloads, potentially leading to information leakage.
enrichment.fix: The path /sys/devices/virtual/powercap is now included in the kubelet's default masked paths, preventing containers from accessing these files.
enrichment.impact: Reduces the attack surface on nodes by blocking a potential power‑based side‑channel leakage, improving security for all pods running on a node.

issueContext.title: JobTemplate validation bug: OnExitCodes should be an optional field for PodFailurePolicyRule
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

[OnExitCodes field should be optional](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/60862c98a4c0bcbc351b076714108d364883b5f7/staging/src/k8s.io/api/batch/v1/types.go#L238) for a PodFailurePolicyRule. 

However, when trying to create a JobSet programmatically with a JobTemplate that defines a PodFailurePolicy rule for failing a job immediately if the failed pod had condition DisruptionTarget, I get a validation error indicating that `OnExitCodes` cannot be null. I've tried using both `k8s.io/api v0.29.4` and `k8s.io/api v0.30.2` (with matching versions for k8s.io/apimachinery package as well).

Error:
```
$ k apply -f examples/simple/failure-policy.yaml 
The JobSet "failurepolicy" is invalid: 
* spec.replicatedJobs[0].template.spec.podFailurePolicy.rules[0].onExitCodes: Invalid value: "null": spec.replicatedJobs[0].template.spec.podFailurePolicy.rules[0].onExitCodes in body must be of type object: "null"
* <nil>: Invalid value: "null": some validation rules were not checked because the object was invalid; correct the existing errors to complete validation
```

JobSet spec:

```yaml
apiVersion: jobset.x-k8s.io/v1alpha2
kind: JobSet
metadata:
  name: failurepolicy
spec:
  replicatedJobs:
  - name: leader
    replicas: 1
    template:
      spec:
        # Set backoff limit to 0 so job will immediately fail if any pod fails.
        backoffLimit: 0
        completions: 2
        parallelism: 2
        template:
          spec:
            restartPolicy: Never
            containers:
            - name: leader
              image: bash:latest
              command:
              - bash
              - -xc
              - |
                for i in $(seq 1 1000)
                do
                  echo "$i"
                  sleep 1
                done
        podFailurePolicy:
          rules:
          - action: FailJob
            onPodConditions:
            - type: DisruptionTarget
```

### W

enrichment.problem: The PodFailurePolicyRule's optional field `onExitCodes` was treated as required during Job (and JobSet) validation, causing a "null" validation error when omitted.
enrichment.affected: Users creating Jobs or JobSets that define a PodFailurePolicy without an `onExitCodes` rule; any workload relying on optional pod failure policy fields.
enrichment.fix: Added `omitempty` tags to optional fields in the Job API structs so that `onExitCodes` (and other optional fields) can be omitted or set to null without failing validation.
enrichment.impact: Allows users to create Jobs and JobSets with PodFailurePolicy rules that do not specify `onExitCodes`, enabling correct usage of the policy feature and preventing spurious validation failures.

Similar issue reported in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/124540 but different struct field.

### What did you expect to happen?

CRD is applied successfully.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create CRD that has PodStatus and then apply it.

bugOrRegression.author: mprahl

bugOrRegression.description: Reverted a [change](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123513) where `ConsistentListFromCache` was moved to beta and enabled by default.

bugOrRegression.description: mount-utils: treated syscall.ENODEV as corrupted mount.

bugOrRegression.description:
Changed how the API server handles updates to `.spec.defaultBackend` of Ingress objects.
Server-side apply now considers `.spec.defaultBackend` to be an atomic struct.  This means that any field-owner who sets values in that struct (they are mutually exclusive) owns the whole struct. For almost all users this change has no impact; for controllers that want to change the default backend port from number to name (or vice-versa), this makes it easier.

issueContext.title: Using server-side-apply for an Ingress failed when updating IngressBackend from port number to port name
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

I created an Ingress resource with a port number manually, and then tried to use an Operator with server-side apply to update the resource from a port number to a port name. This failed with the error message "cannot set both port name & port number".

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected the port number to be cleared as the operator would take over the ownership of the ServiceBackendPort. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

To simulate the behavior in the operator in a most simple example I use `kubectl`:

ingress-v1.yaml:

```
kind: Ingress
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: myingress
spec:
  defaultBackend:
    service:
      name: myservice
      port:
        number: 8443
```

ingress-v2.yaml:

```
kind: Ingress
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: myingress
spec:
  defaultBackend:
    service:
      name: myservice
      port:
        name: http
```

```
kubectl apply -f  ingress-v1.yaml --server-side --field-manager=app-1 --validate=false
kubectl apply -f  ingress-v2.yaml --server-side --field-manager=app-2 --validate=false  --force-conflicts 
```

This will print: 

> The Ingress "myingress" is invalid: spec.defaultBackend: Invalid value: "": cannot set both port name & port number


### Anything else we need to know?

It seems to me that the merge type for the struct ServiceBackendPort should to be set to "atomic" [according to this doc](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/server-side-apply/#merge-strategy), so that the Operator updating the port  should take over the whole struct, and two applications shouldn't update single fields in it.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0cc57258c3f8545c8250f0e7a1307fd01b0d283d/staging/src/k8s.io/api/networking/v1/types.go#L523-L544

### Kubernetes version

```
$ kubectl version
Client Version: v1.30.2
Kustomize Version: v5.0.4-0.20230601165

enrichment.problem: Server-side apply could not update an Ingress object's .spec.defaultBackend when changing the ServiceBackendPort from a numeric port to a named port (or vice versa), producing a "cannot set both port name & port number" error.
enrichment.affected: Operators or controllers that manage Ingress resources via server-side apply, especially when switching default backend ports between numeric and named forms.
enrichment.fix: The API server now treats .spec.defaultBackend as an atomic struct. The field-owner that sets any field in this struct owns the entire struct, allowing seamless transitions between port name and port number without conflict errors.
enrichment.impact: Controllers, operators, and users that use server-side apply to modify Ingress default backends can now change port representations without manual workarounds, reducing failures and simplifying configuration management.

apiChange.description:
Supported fine-grained supplemental groups policy (KEP-3619), which enabled
fine-grained control for supplementary groups in the first container processes.
This allows you to choose whether to include groups defined in the container image (/etc/groups)
for the container's primary UID or not.
apiChange.author: everpeace
apiChange.userFacingChange: Support fine-grained supplemental groups policy (KEP-3619), which enables fine-grained control for supplementary groups in the first container processes. You can choose whether to include groups defined in the container image(/etc/groups) for the container's primary uid or not.

enrichment.problem: Containers always inherited all supplementary groups from the image's /etc/group for the primary UID, preventing users from excluding unnecessary groups and potentially leading to over‑privileged processes.
enrichment.affected: Pods that rely on precise group membership, especially security‑sensitive workloads, and operators configuring pod security contexts.
enrichment.fix: Introduces a fine‑grained supplemental‑groups policy (KEP‑3619) allowing users to specify whether groups defined in the container image should be added to the primary UID's supplementary group set for the first container process.
enrichment.impact: Provides tighter security and privilege isolation for workloads by letting admins opt‑out of unwanted group memberships, reducing the attack surface and aligning container group handling with least‑privilege best practices.

apiChange.description: Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA): Added a feature so the number of ResourceClaim objects can be limited per namespace and by the number of devices requested through a specific class via the v1.ResourceQuota mechanism.
apiChange.author: pohly
apiChange.userFacingChange: DRA: the number of ResourceClaim objects can be limited per namespace and by the number of devices requested through a specific class via the v1.ResourceQuota mechanism.

issueContext.title: dynamic resource allocation: quota = limit number of resource claims per namespace
issueContext.body:
As discussed [in the KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/3063-dynamic-resource-allocation#user-permissions-and-quotas), most likely useful quotas need to be implemented by resource drivers because only they know how much resources get consumed by a specific claim.

What can be limited in Kubernetes itself is the number of ResourceClaims per namespace. For this, two new ResourceQuota resource names get added:

* ` resourceclaims` limits the number of ResourceClaim objects in a namespace across all resource class.
* `<resource-class-name>.resourceclass.node.k8s.io/resourceclaims` limits the number of ResourceClaim objects for the specific resource class.

enrichment.problem: Admins could not limit the number of Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) ResourceClaim objects in a namespace or per resource class, making it possible for workloads to create unbounded claims and potentially exhaust node resources.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) and administrators who need to control claim creation per namespace or per resource class.
enrichment.fix: Added support for limiting ResourceClaim objects via the v1.ResourceQuota mechanism. Two new quota names are introduced: `resourceclaims` to cap total claims in a namespace, and `<resource-class-name>.resourceclass.node.k8s.io/resourceclaims` to cap claims for a specific class.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators can now enforce quotas on DRA claims, preventing runaway claim creation, improving resource governance, and aligning DRA with existing quota controls used for pods and other objects.

apiChange.description: component-base/logs: when compiled with Go >= 1.21, component-base will automatically configure the slog default logger together with initializing klog.
apiChange.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: When building Kubernetes components with Go 1.21 or newer, the component-base library did not automatically set up the new slog default logger, leading to missing or inconsistent log output if klog was also used.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes component compiled with Go 1.21+ that uses component-base for logging, particularly those that also use klog.
enrichment.fix: component-base now detects Go >= 1.21 at compile time and automatically configures the slog default logger while initializing klog, ensuring both logging systems are ready without manual setup.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes binaries that depend on component-base (e.g., kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kubelet, controller-manager, kubectl) will have consistent logging behavior out‑of‑the‑box, simplifying troubleshooting and improving observability for developers and operators.

apiChange.description: User can choose a different static policy option `SpreadPhysicalCPUsPreferredOption` to spread cpus across physical cpus for some specific applications
apiChange.author: Jeffwan

enrichment.problem: Before this change, users could not specify a static CPU manager policy that spreads allocated CPUs across physical CPUs (NUMA nodes). This made it difficult to optimize performance for workloads that benefit from physical CPU separation, leading to possible CPU contention and sub‑optimal latency.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that rely on static CPU allocation, especially those sensitive to CPU topology (e.g., high‑performance compute, latency‑critical services). Cluster administrators configuring the kubelet static CPU manager policy are directly impacted.
enrichment.fix: Introduces a new static policy option `SpreadPhysicalCPUsPreferredOption` that, when enabled, attempts to allocate a pod’s CPUs on separate physical CPUs (across NUMA nodes) while still using the static policy semantics.
enrichment.impact: Performance‑sensitive applications can now obtain a more balanced CPU placement, reducing contention and improving latency. Administrators gain finer‑grained control over pod CPU allocation without needing to switch to the dynamic policy.

apiChange.description: Graduated the `DisableNodeKubeProxyVersion` feature gate to beta. By default, the kubelet no longer attempts to set the `.status.kubeProxyVersion` field for its associated Node.
apiChange.author: HirazawaUi

enrichment.problem: The kubelet was still trying to write the deprecated .status.kubeProxyVersion field on Nodes, which is no longer needed and could lead to stale or unnecessary status updates.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running kubelet versions prior to this change that relied on the kubelet populating .status.kubeProxyVersion, as well as any tooling that read that field.
enrichment.fix: Graduated the DisableNodeKubeProxyVersion feature gate to beta and changed the default to disabled, so the kubelet no longer attempts to set the .status.kubeProxyVersion field for its Node.
enrichment.impact: Clusters no longer receive redundant kube-proxy version information, aligning the Node status API with the deprecation plan and reducing unnecessary write traffic to the apiserver.

apiChange.description: Added Coordinated Leader Election as Alpha under the `CoordinatedLeaderElection` feature gate. With the feature enabled, the control plane can use LeaseCandidate objects (coordination.k8s.io/v1alpha1 API group) to participate in a leader election and let the kube-apiserver select the best instance according to some strategy.
apiChange.author: Jefftree
apiChange.userFacingChange: Add Coordinated Leader Election as alpha under the CoordinatedLeaderElection feature gate. With the feature enabled, the control plane can use LeaseCandidate objects (coordination.k8s.io/v1alpha1 API group) to participate in a leader election and let the kube-apiserver select the best instance according to some strategy.

enrichment.problem: Control plane components could only participate in leader election using basic Lease objects, limiting the ability to choose the best instance based on custom criteria and making high‑availability leader selection less flexible.
enrichment.affected: Control‑plane components that rely on leader election (e.g., kube‑controller‑manager, kube‑scheduler, cloud‑controller‑manager) and any custom controllers that adopt the new LeaseCandidate API.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the CoordinatedLeaderElection alpha feature. When enabled, components can create LeaseCandidate objects (coordination.k8s.io/v1alpha1) and the kube‑apiserver selects the leader according to a pluggable strategy, providing coordinated leader election across the control plane.
enrichment.impact: Allows more sophisticated and deterministic leader selection for control‑plane components, improving HA and simplifying operator control over which instance becomes leader. This paves the way for future enhancements and custom strategies.

apiChange.description: When the featuregate AnonymousAuthConfigurableEndpoints is enabled users can update the AuthenticationConfig file with endpoints for with anonymous requests are alllowed.

apiChange.description: PersistentVolumeLastPhaseTransitionTime feature is stable and enabled by default.

issueContext.title: DRA: kubelet: avoid API version dependency
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

In `pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/plugin/noderesources.go` and `api.proto`, kubelet depends on a specific version of the resource.k8s.io API because it needs to receive resource information from a plugin in that format and copies it into a NodeResourceSlice.

It also pulls ResourceClaim and extracts the allocation result for the plugin.

Instead, kubelet should provide a generic REST proxy for NodeResourceSlice and ResourceClaim and let the plugin decide in which version it wants to access those resources. The plugin then must publish its own NodeResourceSlice objects and get the ResourceClaim.

We also need more E2E tests.

### Why is this needed?

The resource.k8s.io API is likely to evolve as while we continue to work on enhancing structured parameters. Allowing a cluster setup where kubelet is several releases behind the control plane and DRA drivers is desirable because updating kubelet is very intrusive.

/sig node
/triage accepted
/priority important-longterm
/lifecycle frozen
/assign

enrichment.problem: The DRA driver DaemonSet may be deployed with a service account lacking the RBAC permissions required to write ResourceSlice objects and read ResourceClaim objects, causing DRA functionality to fail.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that run the Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) driver daemonset, and any workloads that rely on ResourceSlice/ResourceClaim for node‑resource allocation.
enrichment.fix: Deploy the DRA driver DaemonSet using a service account that has been granted the necessary permissions (create/update ResourceSlice and get/list/watch ResourceClaim). Documentation and manifests have been updated to reflect this requirement.
enrichment.impact: Without the correct service‑account permissions, DRA drivers cannot publish NodeResourceSlice data or consume ResourceClaims, leading to failed resource allocation and potential pod scheduling failures for workloads that depend on Dynamic Resource Allocation.

apiChange.description: Promoted `StatefulSetStartOrdinal` to stable. This means `--feature-gates=StatefulSetStartOrdinal=true` are not needed on kube-apiserver and kube-controller-manager binaries and they'll be removed soon following policy at https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-policy/#deprecation.
apiChange.author: pwschuurman
apiChange.userFacingChange: Promote StatefulSetStartOrdinal to stable. This means `--feature-gates=StatefulSetStartOrdinal=true` are not needed on kube-apiserver and kube-controller-manager binaries and they'll be removed soon following policy at https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-policy/#deprecation

enrichment.problem: StatefulSetStartOrdinal was a beta feature requiring the `--feature-gates=StatefulSetStartOrdinal=true` flag on kube-apiserver and kube-controller-manager. Users had to manage this flag and future removal could cause config breakage.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that had `StatefulSetStartOrdinal` enabled via the feature‑gate flag on kube‑apiserver or kube‑controller‑manager. All workloads using StatefulSets benefit from the stable behavior.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate is promoted to stable (GA). The flag is no longer required and will be removed in a future release per the deprecation policy.
enrichment.impact: Clusters no longer need to enable the feature gate, simplifying API server and controller‑manager configuration and preventing breakage when the flag is removed. The StatefulSet ordinal start behavior is now always available.

apiChange.description: Graduated `JobPodFailurePolicy` to GA and locked it to it's default.
apiChange.author: mimowo
apiChange.userFacingChange: Graduate JobPodFailurePolicy to GA and lock

enrichment.problem: JobPodFailurePolicy was previously in beta and configurable, leading to inconsistent handling of pod failures in Jobs and requiring users to set the policy explicitly.
enrichment.affected: All users creating or managing Job workloads; controllers that reconcile Jobs.
enrichment.fix: The policy is graduated to GA and its default setting is locked, making the behavior stable and immutable for all Jobs.
enrichment.impact: Clusters get a stable, default‑locked JobPodFailurePolicy, removing configuration complexity and ensuring consistent retry behavior for Job pods across upgrades.

apiChange.description: Graduate PodDisruptionConditions to GA and lock
apiChange.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: PodDisruptionConditions were in a pre‑GA state, leading to uncertainty and potential incompatibilities for users relying on them to detect pod‑level disruption status.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that checks pod status for disruption information (e.g., controllers, operators, monitoring tools).
enrichment.fix: Graduated PodDisruptionConditions to GA and made the fields immutable (locked), providing a stable, supported API for pod disruption information.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now reliably use the new pod conditions for automation, monitoring, and graceful handling of disruptions, without fearing future breaking changes.

apiChange.description: Added a `.status.features.supplementalGroupsPolicy` field to Nodes. The field is true when the feature is implemented in the CRI implementation (KEP-3619).
apiChange.author: everpeace
apiChange.userFacingChange: Added Node.Status.Features.SupplementalGroupsPolicy field which is set to true when the feature is implemented in the CRI implementation (KEP-3619)

enrichment.problem: There was no way for users or components to discover whether a node's CRI implementation supports the supplemental groups policy feature (KEP-3619), making it difficult to validate security context capabilities across nodes.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators, developers, and any components that need to verify node support for supplemental groups policy (e.g., custom schedulers, admission controllers).
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new `node.status.features.supplementalGroupsPolicy` boolean field. The kubelet sets this field to true when the underlying CRI reports support for the supplemental groups policy, and the apiserver stores the value in the Node object.
enrichment.impact: Consumers (e.g., schedulers, admission controllers, operators) can now programmatically check node capability and make informed decisions about pod security contexts, improving reliability and security posture of workloads that rely on supplemental groups.

apiChange.description: Enhanced the Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) with an updated version of the resource.k8s.io API group. The primary user-facing type remains the ResourceClaim, however significant changes have been made, resulting in the new version, v1alpha3, which is not compatible with the previous version.
apiChange.author: pohly
apiChange.userFacingChange: DRA: new API and several new features

enrichment.problem: The Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) API version was bumped to v1alpha3, which is not backward‑compatible with the previous version. Clusters and workloads that use ResourceClaim objects must update their manifests and client code to the new API version, otherwise they will encounter validation errors or missing functionality.
enrichment.affected: Clusters and workloads that use the Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) API, including users of ResourceClaim objects, as well as administrators upgrading clusters to a version that includes v1alpha3.
enrichment.fix: Introduces a new version of the resource.k8s.io API group (v1alpha3) with additional features and breaking changes. The API server now serves the new version, and the DRA controller and scheduler plugins have been updated to understand the new schema. Users need to migrate their ResourceClaim definitions to the new version.
enrichment.impact: Enables new DRA capabilities (e.g., richer device resource specifications) for workloads, but requires a migration step for existing clusters. Without migration, workloads that rely on DRA will fail to schedule or be rejected by the API server.

apiChange.description:
kube-apiserver: Added Alpha features to allow API server authz to check the context of requests:
- The `AuthorizeWithSelectors` feature gate enables including field and label selector information from requests in webhook authorization calls.
- The `AuthorizeNodeWithSelectors` feature gate changes node authorizer behavior to limit requests from node API clients, so that each Node can only get / list / watch its own Node API object, and can also only get / list / watch Pod API objects bound to that node. Clients using kubelet credentials to read other nodes or unrelated pods must change their authentication credentials (recommended), adjust their usage, or obtain broader read access independent of the node authorizer.
apiChange.author: liggitt
apiChange.userFacingChange:
kube-apiserver: Added alpha features to allow API server authz to check the context of requests:
- The `AuthorizeWithSelectors` feature gate enables including field and label selector information from requests in webhook authorization calls.
- The `AuthorizeNodeWithSelectors` feature gate changes node authorizer behavior to limit requests from node API clients, so that each Node can only get / list / watch its own Node API object, and can also only get / list / watch Pod API objects bound to that node. Clients using kubelet credentials to read other nodes or unrelated pods must change their authentication credentials (recommended), adjust their usage, or obtain broader read access independent of the node authorizer.

enrichment.problem: Node authorizer permitted kubelet credentials to read any Node or Pod objects, lacking context‑aware checks and risking over‑privileged access.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where kubelet credentials are used to read Node or Pod resources beyond the node's own objects; operators of such clusters.
enrichment.fix: Introduced two alpha feature gates: `AuthorizeWithSelectors` adds field/label selector data to webhook authorizations, and `AuthorizeNodeWithSelectors` restricts node API clients so a node can only GET/LIST/WATCH its own Node object and Pods bound to it. Users must adjust credentials or permissions if they need broader reads.
enrichment.impact: Provides finer‑grained, context‑aware authorization, improving cluster security. Clusters using kubelet credentials to read other nodes or unrelated pods may need to update authentication or RBAC configurations.

apiChange.description: Revised the Pod API with Alpha support for volumes derived from OCI artifacts. This feature is behind the `ImageVolume` feature gate.
apiChange.author: saschagrunert

enrichment.problem: Pods could not reference volumes that are built from OCI artifacts, limiting the ability to use container images as data sources for volumes.
enrichment.affected: Any users or controllers that create Pods and want to use OCI‑artifact‑based volumes; developers testing or adopting the ImageVolume feature gate.
enrichment.fix: The Pod API was revised to add an alpha ImageVolume type, allowing volumes to be derived from OCI artifacts when the ImageVolume feature gate is enabled.
enrichment.impact: Enables new workload patterns where container images can be mounted as read‑only data volumes, simplifying distribution of data and configuration without needing separate CSI drivers or ConfigMaps.

apiChange.description: Promoted `LocalStorageCapacityIsolation` to beta; the behaviour is enabled by default. Within the kubelet, storage capacity isolation is active if the feature gate is enabled and the specific Pod is using a user namespace.
apiChange.author: PannagaRao
apiChange.userFacingChange: Promote LocalStorageCapacityIsolation to beta and enable if user namespace is enabled for the pod

enrichment.problem: Pods running in user namespaces were not subject to local storage capacity isolation, allowing them to consume unlimited node-local storage and potentially impact other workloads.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use a user namespace (e.g., rootless containers) on nodes running the kubelet. The change also affects cluster administrators who rely on storage isolation guarantees.
enrichment.fix: Promoted the LocalStorageCapacityIsolation feature to beta and enabled it by default in the kubelet. The kubelet now enforces storage capacity isolation for any pod that has a user namespace enabled.
enrichment.impact: Improves node stability and multi‑tenant safety by ensuring pods with user namespaces cannot exceed their allocated local storage, providing more reliable storage quota enforcement for workloads such as rootless containers.

apiChange.description: Introduced a new boolean kubelet flag `--fail-cgroupv1`.
apiChange.author: harche
apiChange.userFacingChange: Introduce a new boolean kubelet flag --fail-cgroupv1

enrichment.problem: Clusters migrating away from cgroup v1 need a way to ensure kubelet does not fall back to cgroup v1, but previously there was no explicit flag to stop the kubelet from starting when cgroup v1 is present.
enrichment.affected: Kubelet on nodes that are still using cgroup v1; operators who need to enforce cgroup v2.
enrichment.fix: Adds a new boolean kubelet flag `--fail-cgroupv1`. When set, the kubelet will abort startup if it detects cgroup v1, forcing operators to use cgroup v2.
enrichment.impact: Prevents nodes from unintentionally running with deprecated cgroup v1, helping clusters enforce the cgroup v2 maintenance mode and avoiding potential runtime incompatibilities later.

apiChange.description: Add UserNamespaces field to NodeRuntimeHandlerFeatures
apiChange.author: sohankunkerkar

enrichment.problem: There was no way for the Kubernetes API to convey whether a node's container runtime supports user namespaces, preventing users and controllers from detecting or gating this capability.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where workloads need user namespace support and operators managing node runtime capabilities.
enrichment.fix: Introduces a new `UserNamespaces` boolean field in the `NodeRuntimeHandlerFeatures` API object, allowing the node to report support for user namespaces.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators and workloads that rely on user namespaces can now discover support via the API and make informed scheduling or security decisions, improving workload isolation and feature gating.

apiChange.description:
Graduated the Job `successPolicy` field to beta.

The new reason label, "SuccessPolicy" and "CompletionsReached" are added to the "jobs_finished_total" metric.
Additionally, if you enable the `JobSuccessPolicy` feature gate, the Job gets "CompletionsReached" reason for the "SuccessCriteriaMet" and "Complete" condition type
when the number of succeeded Job Pods (`.status.succeeded`) reached the desired completions (`.spec.completions`).
apiChange.author: tenzen-y
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Graduate the Job SuccessPolicy to Beta.

The new reason label, "SuccessPolicy" and "CompletionsReached" are added to the "jobs_finished_total" metric.
Additionally, If we enable the "JobSuccessPolicy" feature gate, the Job gets "CompletionsReached" reason for the "SuccessCriteriaMet" and "Complete" condition type
when the number of succeeded Job Pods (".status.succeeded") reached the desired completions (".spec.completions").

enrichment.problem: Jobs could not be configured with a success policy to define when a Job is considered successful, and there were no metric labels to distinguish completions reached via the success policy.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes users running batch Jobs who need deterministic success handling or want metric visibility into Job completions, especially when enabling the JobSuccessPolicy feature gate.
enrichment.fix: Graduated the `successPolicy` field to beta, added the "SuccessPolicy" and "CompletionsReached" reason labels to the `jobs_finished_total` metric, and when the `JobSuccessPolicy` feature gate is enabled, the Job controller sets the "CompletionsReached" reason for the `SuccessCriteriaMet` and `Complete` condition types when `.status.succeeded` equals `.spec.completions`.
enrichment.impact: Users can now declaratively control Job success criteria and get clearer observability through metrics, enabling more reliable batch workloads and easier troubleshooting.

apiChange.description: Made kube-proxy Windows service control manager integration (`--windows-service`) configurable in v1alpha1 component configuration via `windowsRunAsService` field.
apiChange.author: aroradaman
apiChange.userFacingChange: kube-proxy Windows service control manager integration(--windows-service) is now configurable in v1alpha1 component configuration via `WindowsRunAsService` field

enrichment.problem: kube-proxy on Windows could only be run as a service via the --windows-service flag and this behavior could not be managed through the v1alpha1 component config, making it hard to enable/disable or reconcile desired state.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that run kube-proxy on Windows nodes and need to control the service‑mode behavior.
enrichment.fix: Added a `windowsRunAsService` (exposed as `WindowsRunAsService` in the API) field to the v1alpha1 component configuration, allowing users to control the Windows service control manager integration via config instead of only the command‑line flag.
enrichment.impact: Administrators can now declaratively configure whether kube-proxy runs as a Windows service, simplifying automation, reducing drift, and aligning Windows proxy configuration with the rest of the component config workflow.

apiChange.description:
Reduced state change noise when volume expansion fails. Also mark certain failures as infeasible.

ACTION REQUIRED:  If you are using the `RecoverVolumeExpansionFailure` alpha feature gate
then after upgrading to this release, you need to update some objects.
For any existing PersistentVolumeClaimss with `status.allocatedResourceStatus` set to either
"ControllerResizeFailed" or "NodeResizeFailed", clear the `status.allocatedResourceStatus`.
apiChange.author: gnufied
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Reduce state change noise when volume expansion fails. Also mark certain failures as infeasible.

ACTION REQUIRED: If you are using the RecoverVolumeExpansionFailure alpha feature, after upgrading to this release, existing PVCs with status.allocatedResourceStatus set to "ControllerResizeFailed" or "NodeResizeFailed" should have their status.allocatedResourceStatus cleared.

enrichment.problem: When a PersistentVolumeClaim volume expansion fails, the controller repeatedly records state changes, creating noisy events, and some failure states are not clearly marked as infeasible. This especially affects users who have enabled the RecoverVolumeExpansionFailure alpha feature gate.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the RecoverVolumeExpansionFailure alpha feature gate, and any PVCs that experienced a failed volume expansion (ControllerResizeFailed or NodeResizeFailed).
enrichment.fix: The change suppresses unnecessary state change events for failed expansions and marks certain failure conditions as infeasible. It also updates the handling of the RecoverVolumeExpansionFailure feature so that after upgrade, PVCs with status.allocatedResourceStatus set to "ControllerResizeFailed" or "NodeResizeFailed" must have that field cleared.
enrichment.impact: Reduces event spam and clarifies failure status for volume expansion, making debugging easier. Users with the RecoverVolumeExpansionFailure feature must perform a one‑time manual cleanup of PVC status fields after upgrading.

apiChange.description:
Promoted feature-gate `VolumeAttributesClass` to beta (disabled by default). Users need to enable the feature gate and the `storage.k8s.io/v1beta1` API group to use this feature.
Promoted the VolumeAttributesClass API to beta.
apiChange.author: carlory
apiChange.userFacingChange:
- Promoted feature-gate `VolumeAttributesClass` to beta (disabled by default). Users need to enable the feature gate and the storage v1beta1 group to use this new feature.
- Promoted API `VolumeAttributesClass` and `VolumeAttributesClassList` to `storage.k8s.io/v1beta1`.

enrichment.problem: The VolumeAttributesClass API was only available as an alpha feature and disabled by default, preventing users from leveraging volume attribute classes for storage provisioning.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and developers who need to use VolumeAttributesClass for CSI storage provisioning; they must enable the feature gate and the storage.k8s.io/v1beta1 API group.
enrichment.fix: Promoted the VolumeAttributesClass feature-gate to beta (still disabled by default) and promoted the VolumeAttributesClass and VolumeAttributesClassList resources to the storage.k8s.io/v1beta1 API group. Users can now enable the feature gate and the v1beta1 API to use the new functionality.
enrichment.impact: Enables clusters to adopt VolumeAttributesClass for more flexible storage configuration once the feature gate is enabled, paving the way for future stable support while keeping the feature gated for early adopters.

apiChange.description: To enhance usability and developer experience, CRD validation rules now support direct use of (CEL) reserved keywords as field names in object validation expressions for existing expressions in storage, will fully support runtime in next release for compatibility concern.
apiChange.author: cici37

enrichment.problem: CRD validation expressions could not directly reference fields whose names are reserved CEL keywords, causing validation failures or requiring awkward work‑arounds.
enrichment.affected: Developers authoring CRDs that use CEL validation and any workloads that rely on those CRDs.
enrichment.fix: The CRD validation engine now permits the use of CEL reserved keywords as field names in object validation expressions for rules stored in etcd. Full runtime support will be added in the following release.
enrichment.impact: Users can write clearer, more natural validation rules for CustomResourceDefinitions without renaming fields or adding work‑arounds, improving developer experience and reducing errors.

apiChange.description: Added an `allocatedResourcesStatus` to each container status to indicate the health status of devices exposed by the device plugin.
apiChange.author: SergeyKanzhelev
apiChange.userFacingChange: Add an AllocatedResourcesStatus to each container status to indicate the health status of devices exposed by the device plugin.

enrichment.problem: Container status did not expose the health condition of devices allocated via device plugins, making it hard for users to detect and react to device failures in a pod.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use device plugins for hardware resources such as GPUs, FPGAs, etc., and the operators who need visibility into device health.
enrichment.fix: Introduced an `allocatedResourcesStatus` field in each ContainerStatus, which reports the health status of the devices allocated to that container by the device plugin.
enrichment.impact: Allows users and controllers to monitor the health of device resources (e.g., GPUs, FPGAs) at the container level, improving diagnostics, automated recovery, and overall reliability of workloads that depend on device plugins.

other.description: Exposed the kube-scheduler "/livez" and "/readz" endpoints for health checks that are in compliance with https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/health-checks/#api-endpoints-for-health.
other.author: linxiulei
other.userFacingChange: The kube-scheduler exposes /livez and /readz for health checks that are in compliance with https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/health-checks/#api-endpoints-for-health

issueContext.title: Split /healthz into /livez & /readyz for kube-scheduler
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Quoted from @wojtek-t 's [comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115754#discussion_r1192068894)

Splitting healthz/ into livez/ and readyz/ 



### Why is this needed?

```
I agree that splitting into livez/ and readyz/ is what we need here:

* livez/ inherits the existing behavior of healthz/ [it just becomes true once the component starts]
* readyz/ is failing when the component isn't initialized (i.e. it's only true after informers are already synced)

Now what we get is:

* non-leader with delayed caching will always be non-ready
* non-leader without delayed caching will be ready as soon as its cache initializes
* leader currently initializing can be distinguished from non-leader using the leader-election metrics

```

enrichment.problem: kube-scheduler only had a single /healthz endpoint, which did not distinguish between liveness and readiness and was not aligned with the standardized health check API used by other components.
enrichment.affected: Operators and monitoring systems that health‑check the kube-scheduler, especially during leader election or cache synchronization phases.
enrichment.fix: Adds two new HTTP endpoints, /livez and /readyz, to kube-scheduler. /livez reports true once the scheduler process is running, while /readyz reports true only after the scheduler has synced its informers and is ready to schedule pods.
enrichment.impact: Monitoring and automation tools can now perform separate liveness and readiness probes on the scheduler, matching the Kubernetes health‑check spec. This improves observability, allows more accurate detection of scheduler initialization delays, and aligns the scheduler with other control‑plane components.

other.description: NONE
other.author: liyuerich

enrichment.problem: Not specified
enrichment.affected: Not specified
enrichment.fix: Not specified
enrichment.impact: Not specified

other.description: k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime: Added support for new calls to handle panics and errors in the context where they occur. `PanicHandlers` and `ErrorHandlers` now must accept a context parameter for that. Log output is structured instead of unstructured.
other.author: pohly
other.userFacingChange: k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime: new calls support handling panics and errors in the context where they occur. `PanicHandlers` and `ErrorHandlers` now must accept a context parameter for that. Log output is structured instead of unstructured.

enrichment.problem: PanicHandlers and ErrorHandlers in apimachinery did not receive the execution context, and log output was unstructured, making it difficult to pinpoint where panics or errors originated and to integrate with structured logging pipelines.
enrichment.affected: Any component or library that registers PanicHandlers or ErrorHandlers via k8s.io/apimachinery, including core control-plane components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet) and custom controllers or operators.
enrichment.fix: Introduced new runtime calls that pass a `context.Context` to PanicHandlers and ErrorHandlers. Updated handler signatures to require the context parameter and switched log output to a structured format.
enrichment.impact: Developers can now capture richer diagnostic information (e.g., request IDs, namespaces) when handling panics or errors, improving debugging and observability. Structured logs are easier to ingest by log aggregation systems.

other.description: KEP-1880: Users of the new feature to add multiple service CIDR will use by default a dual-write strategy on the new ClusterIP allocators to avoid the problem of possible duplicate IPs allocated to Services when running skewed kube-apiservers using different allocators. They can opt-out of this behavior by enabled the feature gate DisableAllocatorDualWrite.
other.author: aojea

enrichment.problem: When clusters enable the new multiple Service CIDR feature and run skewed kube-apiserver versions that use different Service IP allocators, the allocators could allocate the same ClusterIP to different Services, leading to IP collisions and service disruptions.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the multiple Service CIDR feature, especially during upgrades where kube-apiserver instances run with different Service IP allocator implementations.
enrichment.fix: The default behavior of the new ClusterIP allocators now uses a dual‑write strategy, ensuring both allocators record allocations and preventing duplicate IP assignments. Users can opt out of this behavior by disabling the DisableAllocatorDualWrite feature gate.
enrichment.impact: Prevents Service IP collisions in clusters that adopt multiple Service CIDRs and perform version‑skewed upgrades, improving service reliability and upgrade safety.

other.description: Kubelet flag `--keep-terminated-pod-volumes` was removed.  This flag was deprecated in 2017.
other.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: The kubelet flag `--keep-terminated-pod-volumes` was removed, causing kubelet startup failures for clusters that still set this deprecated flag.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that had `--keep-terminated-pod-volumes` enabled in kubelet command line or config files; kubelet processes attempting to parse the unknown flag.
enrichment.fix: The flag has been eliminated; kubelet now always follows the default behavior (do not keep terminated pod volumes). Users must remove the flag from their kubelet command line or config.
enrichment.impact: Removes a long‑standing, unused flag, simplifying kubelet configuration and avoiding confusion. Clusters that still reference the flag will need to update their startup scripts, but no runtime behavior changes for others.

other.description: Removed Kubelet flags `--iptables-masquerade-bit` and `--iptables-drop-bit` as they were deprecated in v1.28. in v1.28 and have now been removed entirely.
other.author: carlory
other.userFacingChange: Kubelet flags `--iptables-masquerade-bit` and `--iptables-drop-bit` were deprecated in v1.28 and have now been removed entirely.

enrichment.problem: The kubelet flags `--iptables-masquerade-bit` and `--iptables-drop-bit` were removed. Nodes that still specify these flags in their kubelet configuration will fail to start because the flags are no longer recognized.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes node running kubelet with the deprecated `--iptables-masquerade-bit` or `--iptables-drop-bit` flags. This typically affects custom node provisioning scripts, systemd unit files, or ConfigMap‑based kubelet configs.
enrichment.fix: The change eliminates the deprecated flags entirely. Users must update their kubelet startup scripts, systemd units, or configuration files to stop passing `--iptables-masquerade-bit` and `--iptables-drop-bit`. The kubelet will use its default iptables behavior.
enrichment.impact: Ensures a cleaner kubelet codebase and removes obsolete configuration options. Clusters that remove the flags experience no change; clusters that still use them must modify their configurations to avoid node startup errors.

other.description:
Removed `ENABLE_CLIENT_GO_WATCH_LIST_ALPHA` environment variable from the reflector.
To activate the feature set `KUBE_FEATURE_WatchListClient` environment variable or a corresponding command line option (this works only with binaries that explicitly expose it).
other.author: p0lyn0mial
other.userFacingChange:
Removes `ENABLE_CLIENT_GO_WATCH_LIST_ALPHA` environmental variable from the reflector.
To activate the feature set `KUBE_FEATURE_WatchListClient` environmental variable or a corresponding command line option (this works only binaries that explicitly expose it).

enrichment.problem: The deprecated environment variable ENABLE_CLIENT_GO_WATCH_LIST_ALPHA was still documented/used to enable the watch list client feature, leading to potential confusion and failure when the variable is no longer recognized.
enrichment.affected: Any workloads or components that configured the reflector with ENABLE_CLIENT_GO_WATCH_LIST_ALPHA (e.g., custom controllers, kube-apiserver, kube-controller‑manager, or other binaries using client‑go).
enrichment.fix: The variable is removed from the reflector implementation. The feature can now be enabled only via the KUBE_FEATURE_WatchListClient environment variable or the corresponding command‑line flag (for binaries that expose it).
enrichment.impact: Users must update any scripts, pods, or components that set ENABLE_CLIENT_GO_WATCH_LIST_ALPHA to the new KUBE_FEATURE_WatchListClient variable or CLI option. The change cleans up the feature‑gate surface and prevents reliance on an unsupported flag.

other.description: Migrated the pkg/proxy to use [contextual logging](https://k8s.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/system-logs/#contextual-logging).
other.author: fatsheep9146

enrichment.problem: kube-proxy's logging lacked contextual information, making it difficult for operators to correlate log entries with specific proxy actions or resources.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running kube-proxy, especially when troubleshooting network traffic or proxy‑related failures.
enrichment.fix: Migrated the pkg/proxy codebase to use the new contextual logging framework, embedding structured fields (e.g., request ID, source IP, operation) in all proxy log messages.
enrichment.impact: Improves observability of the network proxy, enabling faster debugging of traffic‑distribution issues and better integration with log aggregation tools.

other.description: Kubelet is no longer able to recover from device manager state file older than 1.20. If the proper recommended upgrade flow is followed, there should be no issue.
other.author: ffromani

enrichment.problem: Kubelet cannot recover when the device manager state file is from a version older than 1.20, causing the node to fail to start or function correctly after an upgrade.
enrichment.affected: Nodes running kubelet that have a device manager state file from Kubernetes <1.20 during an upgrade.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now validates the version of the device manager state file and refuses to load files older than 1.20, requiring operators to follow the recommended upgrade flow (e.g., remove or regenerate the old state file) before starting the updated kubelet.
enrichment.impact: Clusters upgrading from Kubernetes versions prior to 1.20 must ensure the device manager state file is refreshed. This prevents unexpected kubelet crashes or node unavailability during upgrades.

other.description: Updated cni-plugins to v1.4.1.
other.author: saschagrunert

enrichment.problem: Not specified – the release note does not detail any specific issue, but the update likely addresses bugs or regressions in earlier CNI plugin versions.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes clusters that run the bundled CNI plugins (typically clusters using the default networking stack).
enrichment.fix: Upgraded the bundled CNI plugin binaries to version v1.4.1, replacing the previous version with the newer, patched build.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that use the bundled CNI plugins will benefit from bug fixes, stability improvements, and any security patches included in v1.4.1 without requiring manual upgrades.

other.description:
Removed deprecated command flags --volume-host-cidr-denylist
and --volume-host-allow-local-loopback from kube-controller-manager.
other.author: carlory
other.userFacingChange: kube-controller-manager removes deprecated command flags: --volume-host-cidr-denylist and --volume-host-allow-local-loopback

enrichment.problem: kube-controller-manager still accepted the deprecated command flags --volume-host-cidr-denylist and --volume-host-allow-local-loopback. Clusters that continued to use these flags would see the controller manager fail to start or ignore the flags after the upgrade.

of the nft command-line, and kernel 5.13 or later. (For testing/development
purposes, you can use older kernels, as far back as 5.4, if you set the

issueContext.title: kubectl describe uses Endpoints instead of EndpointSlices
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

kubectl describe should use **discoveryv1.EndpointSlice** instead of **v1.Endpoints**.

### Why is this needed?

Almost everything in Kubernetes uses endpoint slices instead of endpoints.
This discussion started from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/123954.

enrichment.problem: kubectl describe service and kubectl describe ingress displayed v1.Endpoints objects, while the rest of the cluster has moved to using discoveryv1.EndpointSlice. This caused inconsistent output, missing information for clusters that rely on EndpointSlices (e.g., large services, multi-zone setups).
enrichment.affected: Any user running `kubectl describe service` or `kubectl describe ingress`, especially in clusters that have EndpointSlice enabled.
enrichment.fix: The commands now retrieve and render discoveryv1.EndpointSlice resources instead of v1.Endpoints, presenting the same slice‑based endpoint data that the rest of the control plane uses.
enrichment.impact: Users get accurate, up‑to‑date endpoint information when describing services or ingresses, aligning CLI output with the cluster's internal representation and supporting large‑scale endpoint scenarios.

other.description: Moved remote CRI implementation from kubelet to `k8s.io/cri-client` repository.
other.author: saschagrunert

enrichment.problem: The remote Container Runtime Interface (CRI) client implementation was tightly coupled within the kubelet codebase, making it harder to maintain, test, and reuse across other projects.
enrichment.affected: Kubelet developers and any tooling that builds against the kubelet repository; runtime integration remains functionally unchanged for clusters.
enrichment.fix: Extracted the remote CRI implementation into its own repository (`k8s.io/cri-client`). The kubelet now depends on this external module, and the code has been removed from the kubelet repo.
enrichment.impact: Improves code modularity, simplifies independent development and testing of the CRI client, and reduces the kubelet code surface. No functional change for end‑users, but it enables faster iteration and clearer ownership of CRI‑related code.

other.description: kubeadm: Removed the deprecated `UpgradeAddonsBeforeControlPlane` feature gate; Ensured that the upgrade of the CoreDNS and kube-proxy addons would not be triggered until all the control plane instances were upgraded.

enrichment.impact: Clusters that still include the ServiceNodePortStaticSubrange feature gate will fail to start or will log unknown flag errors. Removing the flag restores normal startup. No runtime behavior changes for clusters that have already removed the flag.

enrichment.affected: Developers who imported k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers in their code or CI pipelines; any CI builds that reference this package will break until updated.
enrichment.fix: The k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers module has been removed from the staging directory, cleaning up the repository and ending support for that import path.

enrichment.problem: The deprecated annotation `volume.beta.kubernetes.io/mount-options` could be used on PersistentVolumes without any indication that it is deprecated, leading users to rely on functionality that may be removed in the future.

enrichment.fix: The API server now emits a warning when a PersistentVolume is created or updated with the `volume.beta.kubernetes.io/mount-options` annotation, alerting users to the deprecation.

enrichment.problem: When a test suite involving NodePort services failed, the kernel's iptables and conntrack state were not automatically dumped or cleaned up, making debugging difficult and potentially leaving stale rules on the node.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running kube-proxy with NodePort services, especially when executing network end‑to‑end tests.
enrichment.fix: The change adds a detailed dump of iptables chains and conntrack entries for the node on failure, and ensures proper teardown of the test namespace, improving visibility and cleanup of networking state during testing.
enrichment.impact: Operators and developers can now more easily diagnose networking issues related to NodePort services and iptables/conntrack state, reducing time spent on debugging flaky tests or lingering network rules.

other.description: Removed legacy cloud provider integration code (undoing a previous reverted commit).
other.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: Legacy cloud provider integration code remained in the codebase after a prior revert, providing no functional value and risking confusion for users who might expect it to be supported.
enrichment.affected: Clusters or tools that attempted to use the now‑removed legacy cloud provider integration (e.g., older tutorials, custom cloud‑provider implementations).
enrichment.fix: All vestigial cloud provider integration files and related code paths have been removed, fully undoing the reverted commit and cleaning up the repository.
enrichment.impact: The cleanup eliminates dead code, reduces the maintenance surface, and prevents users from inadvertently relying on unsupported cloud provider integration. No functional change for clusters that were already using the external cloud‑controller‑manager.

other.description: kube-controller-manager: the `horizontal-pod-autoscaler-upscale-delay` and `horizontal-pod-autoscaler-downscale-delay` flags have been removed (deprecated and non-functional since v1.12).
other.author: SataQiu

enrichment.problem: The `horizontal-pod-autoscaler-upscale-delay` and `horizontal-pod-autoscaler-downscale-delay` flags existed in kube-controller-manager but have been non-functional since v1.12, leading to potential confusion for users who set them expecting a scaling delay effect.
enrichment.affected: Administrators who configured the removed flags expecting them to influence HPA scaling behavior.
enrichment.fix: Removed the deprecated and non-functional flags from kube-controller-manager. The code paths and flag definitions are eliminated, ensuring the binary no longer accepts these options.
enrichment.impact: Users can no longer specify these flags, eliminating confusion and reducing maintenance overhead. No behavior change for clusters because the flags never had any effect, but configuration validation becomes clearer.

other.description: Updated CNI Plugins to v1.5.0.
other.author: bzsuni
other.userFacingChange: Update CNI Plugins to v1.5.0

enrichment.problem: Clusters were using an older version of the CNI plugins, which could lack recent bug fixes, security updates, and new features.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes cluster that relies on the built‑in CNI plugins for pod networking, especially on fresh installs or upgrades.
enrichment.fix: The CNI plugins bundled with Kubernetes are upgraded to version v1.5.0, bringing the latest upstream improvements to the networking stack.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that install or upgrade Kubernetes will automatically get the newer CNI binaries, improving network reliability, performance, and security without manual intervention.

other.description: Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA): in the `pod.spec.recourceClaims` array, the `source` indirection is no longer necessary. Instead of e.g. `source: resourceClaimTemplateName: my-template`, one can write `resourceClaimTemplateName: my-template`.
other.author: pohly
other.userFacingChange: DRA: in the `pod.spec.recourceClaims` array, the `source` indirection is no longer necessary. Instead of e.g. `source: resourceClaimTemplateName: my-template`, one can write `resourceClaimTemplateName: my-template`.

enrichment.problem: Pod specifications for Dynamic Resource Allocation required an unnecessary `source:` wrapper around `resourceClaimTemplateName`, making manifests more verbose and confusing.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that defines a pod with `spec.resourceClaims` (e.g., Pods, Deployments, StatefulSets) and users writing pod manifests with the old `source:` syntax.
enrichment.fix: The `source` indirection is removed from `pod.spec.resourceClaims`. Users can now specify `resourceClaimTemplateName: my-template` directly without a surrounding `source:` block.
enrichment.impact: Manifests using DRA become simpler and easier to read. No functional behavior changes; only API syntax is streamlined. Existing workloads that included the `source` field continue to work because the field is ignored, but new manifests can omit it.

other.description: `kubectl describe service` now shows internal traffic policy and ip mode of load balancer IP.
other.author: tnqn

enrichment.affected: Kubectl users managing Services with internal traffic policies or load balancer IP modes.
enrichment.fix: The output of `kubectl describe service` now includes fields for the internal traffic policy and the IP mode of the load balancer IP.
enrichment.impact: Users can now easily view and verify these Service configurations directly from the CLI, simplifying troubleshooting and ensuring the intended network behavior.

other.description: kubeadm: Strictly enabled only the supported klog flags, disallowing previously available but unrecommended options. This means that hidden flags about klog (including `--alsologtostderr`, `--log-backtrace-at`, `--log-dir`, `--logtostderr`, `--log-file`, `--log-file-max-size`, `--one-output`, `--skip-log-headers`, `--stderrthreshold` and `--vmodule`) are no longer allowed to be used.
other.author: SataQiu
other.userFacingChange: kubeadm: only enable the klog flags that are still supported for kubeadm, rather than hiding the unwanted flags. This means that the previously unrecommended hidden flags about klog (including `--alsologtostderr`, `--log-backtrace-at`, `--log-dir`, `--logtostderr`, `--log-file`, `--log-file-max-size`, `--one-output`, `--skip-log-headers`, `--stderrthreshold` and `--vmodule`) are no longer allowed to be used.

enrichment.problem: kubeadm allowed unknown and unsupported klog flags (e.g., --log-dir, --vmodule) which could lead to confusing or unsupported logging configurations.
enrichment.affected: Anyone invoking kubeadm with the now‑blocked klog flags, such as operators using custom logging configurations or automation scripts.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now enables only the klog flags that are officially supported and rejects any hidden or unrecommended flags, causing the command to fail if they are used.
enrichment.impact: Users can no longer rely on undocumented klog flags in kubeadm, preventing misconfiguration and aligning logging behavior with supported options. Scripts that used those flags will need to be updated.

other.description: scheduler framework: Allowed PreBind implementations to return Pending and Unschedulable status codes.
other.author: pohly
other.userFacingChange: scheduler framework: PreBind implementations are now allowed to return Pending and Unschedulable status codes.

issueContext.title: Expand UnschedulablePlugins/PendingPlugins to include PreBind plugins
issueContext.body:
Currently, the scheduler honors Unschedulable(AndUnresolvable) or Pending **_only_** from PreFilter, Filter, Reserve, and Permit (WaitOnPermit).
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/types.go#L210-L214

It doesn't expect other extension points to return those statuses and just regard all non-success status as errors, that is, immediately retrying scheduling of Pods.

Actually [DRA](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/e67f889edc4ab278028f6cffd2501bc90a0defcf/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/dynamicresources/dynamicresources.go#L1613) returns Pending at PreBind, which is currently being ignored as described.
So, we should expand UnschedulablePlugins/PendingPlugins to include PreBind plugins. (or maybe all extension points too?)

/cc @pohly 
/sig scheduling
/kind feature

enrichment.problem: The scheduler only treated Pending and Unschedulable status codes from PreFilter, Filter, Reserve, and Permit plugins. PreBind plugins that returned these codes (e.g., the DRA dynamic resources plugin) were ignored, causing the scheduler to treat them as generic errors and immediately retry pod scheduling.
enrichment.affected: Users of custom or built‑in PreBind plugins, especially those implementing Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) or other pre‑binding checks, and the pods they schedule.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler framework now includes PreBind in the lists of plugins that can return Pending and Unschedulable statuses. PreBind implementations can return these status codes, and the scheduler will handle them correctly, deferring or rejecting pod placement as appropriate.
enrichment.impact: Plugins that need to signal that a pod should wait (Pending) or cannot be scheduled (Unschedulable) at the PreBind stage will now be respected. This prevents unnecessary scheduling retries, improves integration of features like Dynamic Resource Allocation, and leads to more accurate pod placement decisions.

enrichment.problem: During watch cache initialization the Cacher could be in a re-initializing state, causing callers to receive a nil error and leading to flaky tests (e.g., TestStoreListResourceVersion) and potential race conditions in production.

issueContext.title: scheduler: Add ctx param and error return to EnqueueExtensions.EventsToRegister()
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

The scheduling framework `EnqueueExtensions.EventsToRegister()` has recently been changed to return `[]ClusterEventWithHint` instead of `ClusterEvent[]`. Since we've broken API anyway, it seems fitting to add a ctx param and error return to it.

So, change

```
EventsToRegister() []ClusterEventWithHint
```

to

```
EventsToRegister(context.Context) ([]ClusterEventWithHint, error)
```

### Why is this needed?

### context parameter

The primary motivation is to be able to use contextual values, such as [logging](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116884). This is particularly important in WebAssembly where tracing, debug or custom config can be passed contextually to the underlying runtime. `EventsToRegister()` is currently the only plugin extension widely used and missing context,

### error return

The primary motivation of this is to allow coherent behavior on error, or to prevent panics. It is true that a native scheduler plugin is unlikely to err or panic creating the list of functions. However, when implemented in WebAssembly, there could be errors invoking the function in the guest VM, and currently, we have to deal with these in an undefined fashion.

enrichment.problem: The EnqueueExtensions.EventsToRegister() method in the scheduler framework lacked a context parameter and error return, limiting its ability to use contextual information (e.g., logging) and to report errors, especially for WebAssembly plugins.
enrichment.affected: Developers of custom scheduler plugins that implement the EnqueueExtensions interface. Their plugins will fail to compile until updated.
enrichment.fix: The method signature was changed to EventsToRegister(context.Context) ([]ClusterEventWithHint, error). Custom scheduler plugins must update their implementations to accept a context argument and handle the possible error return.
enrichment.impact: Custom scheduler plugin developers must recompile their plugins with the new signature. The change enables richer logging, tracing, and proper error handling for plugins, particularly those running in WASM, without affecting the default scheduler behavior.

issueContext.title: Promote Go version to either 1.23.0 or revert to 1.22.x before K8s 1.31
issueContext.body:
sgtm, add an issue labeled as release-blocking and in the milestone to either promote to 1.23.0 or revert this to 1.22.x before our 1.31 release

_Originally posted by @liggitt in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126047#issuecomment-2245648031_

Kubernetes is being built and tested with go1.23rc2 at HEAD (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/126047) to let it bake in the CI and help iron out issues, if any, with this version of Go.

However, for the 1.31 release, the version of Go should be a non-rc, released version. The release timeline of go1.23.0 is ~same as the release timeline of K8s 1.31.0 (see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/126047#issuecomment-2235706834). If go1.23.0 is not out by then, we should revert to go1.22.x before cutting K8s 1.31.0.

/sig release architecture
/area code-organization
/cc @liggitt @dims @cpanato

enrichment.problem: The Kubernetes project was building and testing with Go 1.23rc2, a release candidate, which is not an officially released Go version. For the 1.31 release a stable, non‑RC Go version is required to avoid build‑time regressions and to unblock the release.
enrichment.affected: Anyone building or testing Kubernetes from source, including CI systems and downstream distributors, who would have been affected by the unstable Go 1.23rc2 toolchain.
enrichment.fix: Kubernetes is now built with the stable Go 1.22.5 toolchain for this release, ensuring all binaries are compiled with a supported, non‑RC Go version.
enrichment.impact: Provides a reliable, reproducible build environment for all users and CI pipelines, eliminating potential breakages caused by an unreleased Go version and satisfying the release‑blocker requirement.

issueContext.title: Name of feature gate `DisableKubeletCSRAdmissionValidation` doesn't match other fixups
issueContext.body:
This comes from https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C5P3FE08M/p1722095887026819?thread_ts=1721949988.922209&cid=C5P3FE08M

We've [added](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/126015) a feature gate, `DisableKubeletCSRAdmissionValidation`. However, we try to name feature gates after the positive thing they add, even if it's on by default, or even if we're setting if false because the positive thing is being dropped (rare, but it happens).

Typically we don't start feature gate names with `Disable`, as it makes the docs jar:
Example quote 1: _To temporarily revert to the legacy behavior, enable the_ `DisableFoo` _feature gate._
vs
Example quote 2: _You can enable the_ `LegacyFooHandling` _feature gate if you run code that relies on the previous behavior. You should plan to migrate._

and because disabling things isn't really a feature.

---

Some examples of gates you can or once could disable by turning them _off_ include:

- `AllowInsecureBackendProxy`
- `APIServingWithRoutine`
- `StorageNamespaceIndex`
- `LegacyNodeRoleBehavior`
- `LegacyServiceAccountTokenNoAutoGeneration`
- `LegacyServiceAccountTokenTracking`

So, I recommend a rename of the gate before the v1.31 release.

/sig auth architecture

enrichment.problem: The Node Admission plugin previously allowed CertificateSigningRequest (CSR) objects created by a node identity for the signers `kubernetes.io/kubelet-serving` or `kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client-kubelet` with a common name that began with `system:node:` but did not exactly match `system:node:${node-name}`. This could let a compromised or malicious node obtain valid serving or client certificates for a different node name, enabling node impersonation.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where kubelet or control-plane components create CSRs for kubelet-serving or kube-apiserver-client-kubelet signers. Nodes that previously submitted CSRs with mismatched CNs will have those requests rejected.
enrichment.fix: The admission plugin now validates that the CN of such CSRs exactly matches the node's name (`system:node:${node-name}`). Requests that do not meet this rule are rejected. The feature gate `AllowInsecureKubeletCertificateSigningRequests` defaults to `false` to enforce the new validation, and can be temporarily enabled to retain the legacy behavior. The gate will be removed in v1.33.
enrichment.impact: Improves cluster security by preventing node impersonation through malformed CSRs. Clusters upgrading to this version will see stricter certificate validation, which may require disabling the temporary feature gate if legacy tooling relied on the previous lax behavior. No functional impact on normal node operation.
