kubeadm: deprecated the kubeadm `RootlessControlPlane` feature gate (previously alpha), given that the core K8s `UserNamespacesSupport` feature gate graduated to beta in 1.30.
Once core Kubernetes support for user namespaces is generally available and kubeadm has started to support running the control plane in userns pods, the kubeadm `RootlessControlPlane` feature gate will be removed entirely.
Until kubeadm supports the userns functionality out of the box, users can continue using the deprecated  `RootlessControlPlane` feature gate, or  opt-in `UserNamespacesSupport` by using kubeadm patches on the static pod manifests.
deprecation.author: neolit123
deprecation.userFacingChange:
kubeadm: deprecated the kubeadm `RootlessControlPlane` feature gate (previously alpha), given that the core K8s `UserNamespacesSupport` feature gate graduated to Beta in 1.30.
Once core Kubernetes support for user namespaces is generally available and kubeadm has started to support running the control plane in userns pods, the kubeadm `RootlessControlPlane` feature gate will be removed entirely.
Until kubeadm supports the userns functionality out of the box, users can continue using the deprecated  `RootlessControlPlane` feature gate, or  opt-in `UserNamespacesSupport` by using kubeadm patches on the static pod manifests.

enrichment.problem: The kubeadm `RootlessControlPlane` feature gate, previously alpha, is deprecated now that the core `UserNamespacesSupport` feature gate has graduated to beta. Users relying on this gate may be unaware of its deprecation and the upcoming removal.
enrichment.affected: Users running kubeadm clusters with the `RootlessControlPlane` feature gate enabled, especially those seeking rootless control‑plane deployments.
enrichment.fix: Kubeadm marks `RootlessControlPlane` as deprecated and recommends continuing to use it only until kubeadm natively supports user namespaces, or to opt‑in to `UserNamespacesSupport` by patching the static pod manifests. The gate will be removed once full support is available.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that enable `RootlessControlPlane` must plan to transition to the core `UserNamespacesSupport` feature. Failure to adapt before the gate is removed will prevent rootless control‑plane setups, requiring manual manifest patches or waiting for kubeadm's built‑in support.

deprecation.description: Reverted the `DisableNodeKubeProxyVersion` feature gate to default-off to give a full year from deprecation announcement in 1.29 to clearing the field by default, per the [Kubernetes deprecation policy](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-policy/).
deprecation.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: The `DisableNodeKubeProxyVersion` feature gate was left enabled by default after its deprecation announcement, which did not give users the full one‑year grace period required by the deprecation policy.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that had the `DisableNodeKubeProxyVersion` feature gate enabled (or the field set) expecting it to stay on by default. Administrators managing node‑level proxy configuration are directly impacted.
enrichment.fix: Reverted the feature gate to its default‑off state, ensuring the gate is disabled by default and the corresponding field will be cleared after the one‑year deprecation window.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that relied on the feature gate being enabled by default must now explicitly enable it if needed; otherwise kube‑proxy will operate with the default behavior. This aligns the change with the Kubernetes deprecation policy and prevents unexpected behavior after the deprecation window closes.

apiChange.description: The resource/v1alpha3.ResourceSliceList filed which should have been named "metadata" but was instead named "listMeta" is now properly "metadata".
apiChange.author: thockin

enrichment.problem: The ResourceSliceList type in the v1alpha3 API used the field name "listMeta" instead of the correct "metadata", causing inconsistency with other list types and potentially breaking client code that expects the standard field name.
enrichment.affected: Users of the v1alpha3 ResourceSlice API (e.g., custom controllers, client-go code, kubectl) that create or read ResourceSliceList objects.
enrichment.fix: Renamed the field from "listMeta" to "metadata" in the ResourceSliceList definition so it now follows the conventional API schema.
enrichment.impact: Clients, controllers, and tooling that interact with ResourceSliceList objects will see the correct field name, eliminating confusion and preventing serialization/validation issues. The change restores API consistency and improves developer experience.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.6
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were still being built with an older Go toolchain, missing recent security patches, bug fixes, and performance improvements from newer Go releases.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) because their binaries are rebuilt with the newer Go version.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go version 1.22.6 for compiling all Kubernetes components.
enrichment.impact: All released binaries now include the latest Go runtime security updates and performance improvements, reducing the risk of vulnerabilities and ensuring compatibility with future Go releases.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a scheduler preemption issue where the victim pod was not deleted due to incorrect status patching. This issue occurred when the preemptor and victim pods had different QoS classes in their status, causing the preemption to fail entirely.
bugOrRegression.author: Huang-Wei

enrichment.problem: When a preemptor pod and a victim pod had different QoS classes, the scheduler patched the victim pod's status incorrectly, preventing the victim pod from being deleted and causing the entire preemption attempt to fail.
enrichment.affected: Pods that are preempted when the preemptor and victim have mismatched QoS classes; clusters using pod priority and preemption.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now correctly patches the victim pod’s status regardless of QoS class differences, ensuring the victim pod is deleted and preemption proceeds as expected.
enrichment.impact: Allows high‑priority pods to preempt lower‑priority pods even when they belong to different QoS classes, restoring expected scheduling behavior and preventing scheduling dead‑locks.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix race condition in kube-proxy initialization that could blackhole UDP traffic to service VIP.
bugOrRegression.author: wedaly

enrichment.problem: A race condition during kube-proxy initialization could cause UDP packets to the service virtual IP (VIP) to be dropped, effectively blackholing UDP traffic for services.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running kube-proxy with UDP services; any pod or external client sending UDP to a Service VIP could experience traffic loss.
enrichment.fix: Added proper synchronization in kube-proxy startup to ensure the proxy rules for UDP services are fully established before traffic is accepted, eliminating the race that caused packet loss.
enrichment.impact: UDP‑based services (e.g., DNS, media streaming) will reliably receive traffic after kube-proxy starts, preventing intermittent outages and data loss for workloads relying on UDP.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug where init containers may fail to start due to a temporary container runtime failure.
bugOrRegression.author: SergeyKanzhelev

enrichment.problem: Init containers could fail to start when the container runtime experienced a temporary failure, causing the pod to be stuck in Init:Error.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that use init containers on nodes where the container runtime may have transient issues.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now correctly retries or handles transient container runtime errors during init container startup, preventing unnecessary failures.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on init containers become more reliable; clusters experience fewer pod startup failures and reduced need for manual intervention.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a regression in 1.29+ default configurations, where regular init containers may fail to start due to a temporary container runtime failure.
bugOrRegression.author: SergeyKanzhelev

enrichment.problem: A regression in the default configuration for Kubernetes 1.29+ caused regular init containers to fail to start because of a temporary container runtime failure.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running Kubernetes 1.29+ with default node configurations that use init containers in their pod specs.
enrichment.fix: The regression was corrected so that init containers are started correctly under the default configuration, eliminating the spurious runtime failure.
enrichment.impact: Pods that use init containers will now start reliably in clusters running 1.29+ with default settings, preventing startup delays or pod failures.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: Fixes a 1.31 regression that stopped honoring build ID overrides with the --version flag
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes 1.31, kube-apiserver ignored custom build ID values passed via the --version flag, causing the server to always report its default build ID.
enrichment.affected: Any deployment of kube-apiserver that uses the --version flag to override the build ID was affected; the flag previously had no effect.
enrichment.fix: The regression was corrected so that kube-apiserver now respects and displays the overridden build ID when the --version flag is used.
enrichment.impact: Allows administrators, CI pipelines, and debugging tools to correctly report custom version information, improving observability and consistency in environments that rely on build ID overrides.

bugOrRegression.description: Revert "fix: handle socket file detection on Windows"
bugOrRegression.author: jsturtevant

enrichment.problem: A recent change that added socket file detection handling for Windows introduced regressions, causing node or pod management issues on Windows nodes.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running Windows nodes, specifically the kubelet component that processes socket files.
enrichment.fix: The change is reverted, restoring the previous logic and eliminating the problematic behavior on Windows nodes.
enrichment.impact: Windows workloads regain stability; users who experienced failures after the prior fix can now operate clusters normally. The temporary limitation on socket detection returns, but overall cluster reliability improves.

bugOrRegression.description: Terminated Pods on a node will not be re-admitted on kubelet restart. This fixes the problem of Completed Pods awaiting for the finalizer marked as Failed after the kubelet restart.
bugOrRegression.author: SergeyKanzhelev

enrichment.problem: After a kubelet restart, pods that had already terminated (Completed) were incorrectly re‑admitted and marked as Failed because they were still awaiting a finalizer, causing completed jobs to appear failed.
enrichment.affected: Any workload with Completed pods (such as Jobs) on nodes where the kubelet restarts would see those pods incorrectly marked as Failed.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now ignores terminated pods on restart, ensuring they are not re‑admitted and the finalizer handling completes correctly, so Completed pods remain in their finished state.
enrichment.impact: Prevents false failure reporting for batch workloads (e.g., Jobs) and improves pod lifecycle reliability after node restarts, reducing unnecessary pod recreation and operator confusion.

bugOrRegression.description: Upgrade coreDNS to v1.11.3
bugOrRegression.author: BenTheElder

enrichment.problem: Clusters running older CoreDNS versions may encounter DNS bugs, reduced reliability, or unpatched security issues.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes clusters using the CoreDNS add‑on; affects pods and services that perform DNS lookups.
enrichment.fix: Upgrade the CoreDNS add‑on to version v1.11.3, which includes bug fixes and security patches.
enrichment.impact: Improves DNS reliability and security for all workloads that rely on cluster DNS, reducing the risk of service‑discovery failures.

other.description: Updated cni-plugins to [v1.5.1](https://github.com/containernetworking/plugins/releases/tag/v1.5.1).
other.author: saschagrunert

enrichment.problem: Previous version of the CNI plugins (prior to v1.5.1) contained bugs and potential security issues that could cause networking instability or expose clusters to vulnerabilities.
enrichment.affected: All clusters using the default CNI plugins for pod networking, especially workloads that create or modify network interfaces.
enrichment.fix: The release upgrades the bundled CNI plugins to version v1.5.1, which includes bug fixes, security patches, and stability improvements.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that rely on the built‑in CNI plugins will have more reliable pod networking and reduced security risk. No manual action is required beyond the upgrade.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.7
feature.author: haitch

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version; the release needed to update the toolchain to Go 1.22.7.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components compiled from source (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) are rebuilt with Go 1.22.7.
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes components are now compiled using Go 1.22.7, updating the build environment across the codebase.
enrichment.impact: Ensures compatibility with the latest Go language improvements, security patches, and performance optimizations. Future builds and downstream distributions will benefit from the updated toolchain without requiring user action.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.8
feature.author: haitch

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes builds were using an older Go toolchain, which could cause build failures or incompatibilities with newer Go versions.
enrichment.affected: Users who compile Kubernetes from source; CI pipelines that build Kubernetes binaries.
enrichment.fix: The source tree is now compiled with Go 1.22.8, updating the build toolchain across all components.
enrichment.impact: Developers building Kubernetes from source will have a smoother, more reliable build process and benefit from Go 1.22's improvements and security patches. No runtime behavior changes for existing clusters.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a bug on the endpoints controller that does not reconcile the Endpoint object after this is truncated (it gets more than 1000 endpoints addresses)
bugOrRegression.author: aojea

enrichment.problem: When a Service has more than 1000 endpoint addresses, the endpoints controller truncates the list but fails to update (reconcile) the corresponding Endpoint object, leaving stale or incomplete endpoint data.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running Services that generate >1000 endpoints (e.g., large Deployments, StatefulSets). The stale Endpoint objects could cause misrouted or dropped traffic.
enrichment.fix: The endpoints controller now triggers a reconciliation after truncation, ensuring the Endpoint object is updated with the truncated address set.
enrichment.impact: Services with large numbers of pods will have correct endpoint information, preventing traffic routing failures and ensuring reliable service discovery for workloads that rely on many endpoints.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a 1.31 regression with API emulation versioning honors cohabitating resources
bugOrRegression.author: xuzhenglun

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced in Kubernetes 1.31 caused the API emulation versioning logic to ignore the presence of cohabitating resources, leading to incorrect version negotiation for those resources.
enrichment.affected: Users and controllers interacting with the kube-apiserver when using resources that share storage but have multiple API versions (cohabitating resources).
enrichment.fix: The regression was fixed by restoring the correct handling of cohabitating resources in the API emulation versioning code, ensuring version negotiation respects all coexisting resource versions.
enrichment.impact: Clients and controllers that depend on accurate API versioning for cohabitating resources will now receive the correct version, avoiding request failures and incompatibility issues.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a kubelet and kube-apiserver memory leak in default 1.29 configurations related to tracing.
bugOrRegression.author: dashpole

enrichment.problem: A memory leak existed in the tracing implementation of kubelet and kube-apiserver under the default 1.29 configuration, causing continuous memory growth that could eventually lead to out‑of‑memory crashes.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes 1.29 cluster that uses the default tracing configuration, affecting both the control‑plane (kube‑apiserver) and worker nodes (kubelet).
enrichment.fix: The leak was eliminated by fixing the tracing code paths in both kubelet and kube-apiserver, ensuring memory is correctly released when tracing data is no longer needed.
enrichment.impact: Clusters running the default 1.29 configuration will see stable memory usage for kubelet and apiserver, preventing potential node or control‑plane outages and improving overall cluster reliability.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fixes a regression introduced in 1.29 where conntrack entries for UDP connections
  to deleted pods did not get cleaned up correctly, which could (among other things)
  cause DNS problems when DNS pods were restarted.
bugOrRegression.author: danwinship

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes 1.29 a regression caused conntrack entries for UDP connections targeting pods that had been deleted to remain in the kernel, preventing proper cleanup. This could lead to stale NAT entries and DNS resolution failures when DNS pods were restarted.
enrichment.affected: All workloads using UDP connections, particularly DNS pods, could be impacted by failed DNS queries after pod restarts.
enrichment.fix: The regression was fixed by ensuring that when a pod is deleted, any associated UDP conntrack entries are correctly removed, restoring proper traffic flow and DNS functionality.
enrichment.impact: Prevents DNS outages and other UDP connectivity problems caused by stale conntrack state, improving cluster reliability especially during DNS pod restarts or frequent pod churn.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: ensure that Pods from the upgrade preflight check `CreateJob` are properly terminated after a timeout.
bugOrRegression.author: yuyabee

enrichment.problem: During a kubeadm upgrade, the preflight check creates a Job pod (CreateJob) that is not terminated if it exceeds its timeout, leaving stray pods and potentially blocking the upgrade process.
enrichment.affected: Clusters upgraded with kubeadm that run the upgrade preflight checks. Users performing kubeadm upgrade could see stuck pods if the timeout occurred.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now tracks the timeout of the preflight Job and explicitly deletes the associated pod(s) when the timeout is reached, ensuring proper cleanup.
enrichment.impact: Prevents resource leakage and upgrade hangs caused by lingering preflight pods, making kubeadm upgrade workflows more reliable and predictable.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix wrong member list reported when removing an etcd member
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu

enrichment.problem: When an etcd member was removed using kubeadm, the command reported an incorrect member list, showing stale or missing entries.
enrichment.affected: Clusters managed with kubeadm that perform etcd member removal; operators relying on the reported member list.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now updates and displays the correct etcd member list after a removal operation.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators receive an accurate view of the etcd cluster membership, avoiding confusion during scaling, upgrades, or troubleshooting.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: when adding new control plane nodes with "kubeadm join", ensure that the etcd member addition is performed only if a given member URL does not already exist in the list of members. Similarly, on "kubeadm reset" only remove an etcd member if its ID exists.
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu

enrichment.problem: kubeadm join could attempt to add an etcd member that was already present, and kubeadm reset could try to remove a non‑existent etcd member, leading to errors during control‑plane node provisioning or cluster reset.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use kubeadm to join new control‑plane nodes or perform kubeadm reset, especially those with pre‑existing etcd members.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now checks the existing etcd member list: it adds a member only if its URL is not already in the cluster, and during reset it removes a member only if its ID is present.
enrichment.impact: Prevents join or reset failures caused by duplicate or missing etcd member operations, making control‑plane node addition and cluster teardown more reliable.

other.description: Kubeadm: removed `socat` and `ebtables` from kubeadm preflight checks
other.author: saschagrunert

enrichment.problem: kubeadm preflight checks required the presence of the `socat` and `ebtables` binaries, causing init/join to fail on systems where these tools are not needed or not installed.
enrichment.affected: Clusters being provisioned with kubeadm on nodes that do not have `socat` or `ebtables` installed, especially in environments that do not rely on ebtables‑based networking.
enrichment.fix: The preflight logic was updated to no longer check for `socat` and `ebtables`, so kubeadm can proceed without those binaries being present.
enrichment.impact: Users can now run `kubeadm init` or `kubeadm join` without having to install unnecessary networking utilities, reducing setup friction and preventing false‑positive preflight failures.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a bug when the hostname label of a node does not match the node name, pods bound to a PV with nodeAffinity using the hostname may be scheduled to the wrong node or experience scheduling failures.
bugOrRegression.author: AxeZhan

enrichment.problem: When a node's hostname label (kubernetes.io/hostname) does not match the node's name, pods that are bound to a PersistentVolume with nodeAffinity using the hostname label could be scheduled onto the wrong node or fail to schedule.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that use PersistentVolumes with nodeAffinity on the hostname label, and clusters where node hostname labels differ from node names.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now correctly interprets the hostname label even when it differs from the node name, ensuring that nodeAffinity rules based on the hostname label are applied to the intended node.
enrichment.impact: Pods using PVs with hostname‑based nodeAffinity are reliably placed on the correct node, preventing scheduling failures and potential storage access issues, improving cluster stability for stateful workloads.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a suboptimal scheduler preemption behavior where potential preemption victims were violating Pod Disruption Budgets.
bugOrRegression.author: NoicFank

enrichment.problem: The scheduler could preempt pods that were protected by Pod Disruption Budgets (PDBs), causing unnecessary violations of those budgets during preemption.
enrichment.affected: Workloads using Pod Disruption Budgets and any cluster that performs priority‑based preemption.
enrichment.fix: Scheduler preemption logic was updated to filter out potential victims that would breach a PDB, ensuring preemption respects PDB constraints.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that rely on PDBs for graceful disruption now avoid unintended pod evictions during preemption, improving workload stability and reducing disruption risk.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes 1.31 regression that can crash kube-controller-manager's service-lb-controller loop
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced in Kubernetes 1.31 could cause the kube-controller-manager's service load‑balancer controller loop to panic and crash, stopping the controller that reconciles Service resources with cloud provider load balancers.
enrichment.affected: Clusters upgraded to or running Kubernetes 1.31 where the service‑lb‑controller is enabled, especially those using cloud provider load balancer integration.
enrichment.fix: The patch restores the previous safe behavior in the service‑lb‑controller, preventing the panic and ensuring the controller loop continues running.
enrichment.impact: Prevents unexpected controller‑manager crashes, keeping Service load‑balancer provisioning operational and maintaining overall cluster stability for users relying on cloud provider load balancers.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.9
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes was previously built with an older Go toolchain, which could miss security patches, bug fixes, and language improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) are rebuilt with Go 1.22.9.
enrichment.fix: The release updates the build process to use Go 1.22.9, rebuilding all Kubernetes binaries with the newer compiler and standard library.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes components are now compiled with a newer, supported Go version, improving binary security, stability, and compatibility with future Go releases.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix bug where PodCIDR was released before node was deleted
bugOrRegression.author: adrianmoisey

enrichment.problem: When a node was deleted, its allocated PodCIDR was released back to the address pool before the node object was fully removed, risking IP address collisions for pods on the deleted node.
enrichment.affected: Clusters performing node deletions; pods running on nodes being removed could experience networking failures due to CIDR reuse.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the deletion workflow so that the PodCIDR is released only after the node deletion is completely processed, ensuring the CIDR remains reserved until the node is fully gone.
enrichment.impact: Prevents pod networking conflicts and IP address reuse errors during node termination, leading to more reliable cluster networking and smoother node scaling operations.

securityFixes.title: Command Injection affecting Windows nodes via nodes/*/logs/query API
securityFixes.description:
A security vulnerability has been discovered in Kubernetes windows nodes
that could allow a user with the ability to query a node's '/logs' endpoint
to execute arbitrary commands on the host.

apiChange.description: NONE

enrichment.problem: Not specified
enrichment.affected: Not specified
enrichment.fix: Not specified
enrichment.impact: Not specified

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.10
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with an older Go version; the release updates the build toolchain to Go 1.22.10.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components built from source, including kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, and kubectl.
enrichment.fix: The build process is modified to compile all Kubernetes components with Go 1.22.10.
enrichment.impact: Users receive binaries that include Go security patches and performance improvements, ensuring better upstream security and future compatibility without changing runtime behavior.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a storage bug around multipath. iSCSI and Fibre Channel devices attached to nodes via multipath now resolve correctly if partitioned.
bugOrRegression.author: RomanBednar

enrichment.problem: When iSCSI or Fibre Channel devices were attached to nodes via multipath and had partitions, the device path resolution failed, causing volume attach/mount errors.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes nodes using iSCSI or Fibre Channel devices attached via multipath with partitions; workloads that need those volumes.
enrichment.fix: Implemented correct handling of partitioned multipath devices, ensuring that iSCSI and Fibre Channel devices resolve properly during attach and mount operations.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on iSCSI or Fibre Channel storage through multipath will now mount volumes successfully, preventing startup failures and potential data access issues.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a panic in kube-controller-manager handling StatefulSet objects when revisionHistoryLimit is negative
bugOrRegression.author: ardaguclu

enrichment.problem: kube-controller-manager panics when it processes a StatefulSet that has a negative revisionHistoryLimit, causing the controller manager to crash.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where a StatefulSet is created or updated with a negative revisionHistoryLimit value; the controller manager would panic and restart.
enrichment.fix: Added a guard/validation in the StatefulSet handling code to detect and safely ignore negative revisionHistoryLimit values, preventing the panic.
enrichment.impact: Prevents controller-manager crashes for clusters with malformed StatefulSet specifications, improving cluster stability and control loop reliability.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix a bug where the 'node.skipPhases' in UpgradeConfiguration is not respected by 'kubeadm upgrade node' command
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: The `node.skipPhases` setting in `UpgradeConfiguration` was ignored by the `kubeadm upgrade node` command, causing all upgrade phases to run even when users intended to skip some.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators using `kubeadm upgrade node` with a custom `UpgradeConfiguration` that includes `node.skipPhases`.
enrichment.fix: The `kubeadm upgrade node` implementation was updated to honor the `node.skipPhases` configuration, skipping the specified phases during a node upgrade.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators can now reliably skip selected upgrade phases, reducing unnecessary work and avoiding unintended changes during node upgrades.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubelet: Fix the volume manager didn't check the device mount state in the actual state of the world before marking the volume as detached. It may cause a pod to be stuck in the Terminating state due to the above issue when it was deleted.
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: The kubelet’s volume manager marked a volume as detached without first verifying that the device was still mounted in the actual state of the world. When a pod using that volume was deleted, the pod could become stuck in the Terminating phase.
enrichment.affected: Any pod that uses a volume and is deleted could be impacted, leading to pods remaining stuck in Terminating state on the node.
enrichment.fix: Added a check of the device’s mount state in the actual state of the world before marking the volume as detached, ensuring the volume is only considered detached after it is truly unmounted.
enrichment.impact: Pods that are deleted now terminate correctly instead of remaining indefinitely in the Terminating state, improving reliability of pod lifecycle management and preventing stale resources from accumulating on nodes.

securityFixes.title: Node Denial of Service via Kubelet Checkpoint API
securityFixes.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a large number of container checkpoint requests made to the unauthenticated kubelet read-only HTTP endpoint may cause a Node Denial of Service by filling the Node's disk.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.11
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with an older Go version; this could miss upstream Go security and stability fixes.
enrichment.affected: Developers and organizations that compile Kubernetes from source, CI/CD pipelines, and downstream binary distributors.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.22.11 for compiling Kubernetes.
enrichment.impact: Clusters built from source or maintained by distributors will benefit from Go security patches, bug fixes, and performance improvements, reducing the risk of upstream Go vulnerabilities affecting the Kubernetes binaries.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.12
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Not applicable – this change is not a bug fix but an upgrade of the Go toolchain used to compile Kubernetes binaries.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) are rebuilt with the newer Go version.
enrichment.fix: The Kubernetes build system has been updated to use Go version 1.22.12 for compiling all components.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes binaries are now built with a newer, supported Go release, bringing compiler bug fixes, security patches, and newer language/runtime features. This improves reliability of future builds and aligns with upstream Go maintenance policies.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix nil pointer panic in BuildOpenAPIV2 and BuildOpenAPIV3 utilities, used by kube-apiserver's openAPI controller, when a CRD is missing version the requested version.
bugOrRegression.author: jpbetz

enrichment.problem: kube-apiserver could panic with a nil pointer in the BuildOpenAPIV2 and BuildOpenAPIV3 utilities when a CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) does not contain the version that the OpenAPI controller requests.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that have CRDs lacking the requested version, typically affecting cluster administrators and workloads that rely on the API server’s OpenAPI endpoints.
enrichment.fix: Added defensive nil checks and version‑presence validation in the OpenAPI building utilities so that missing CRD versions are handled gracefully instead of causing a panic.
enrichment.impact: Prevents kube-apiserver crashes caused by malformed or incomplete CRDs, ensuring the API server remains available and OpenAPI discovery continues to work.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed in-tree to CSI migration for Portworx volumes, in clusters where Portworx security feature is enabled (it's a Portworx feature, not Kubernetes feature). It required secret data from the secret mentioned in-tree SC, to be passed in CSI requests which was not happening before this fix.
bugOrRegression.author: gohilankit

enrichment.problem: When migrating in-tree Portworx volumes to CSI in clusters with the Portworx security feature enabled, the secret data defined in the original in-tree StorageClass was not forwarded to the CSI driver, causing provisioning/attachment failures.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters that have Portworx storage with the security feature enabled and are performing in-tree to CSI migration for those volumes.
enrichment.fix: The migration code now correctly extracts the secret referenced by the in-tree StorageClass and includes it in CSI requests, ensuring the CSI driver receives the required security credentials.
enrichment.impact: Clusters using Portworx with security enabled can successfully migrate to the CSI driver without manual work‑arounds, restoring volume provisioning and attachment functionality.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fixed a bug where an image is not pulled if there is an error with the sandbox image from CRI.
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: When the CRI sandbox image fails, kubeadm does not attempt to pull subsequent container images, causing pod creation to stall.
enrichment.affected: Users initializing clusters with kubeadm, especially those using custom CRI implementations where sandbox image errors may occur.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now continues to pull required images even if the sandbox image lookup returns an error.
enrichment.impact: Clusters bootstrapped with kubeadm are more resilient; pod startup is no longer blocked by sandbox image issues, reducing setup failures and downtime.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fixed the bug where the v1beta4 Timeouts.EtcdAPICall field was not respected in etcd client operations, and the default timeout of 2 minutes was always used.
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: kubeadm ignored the v1beta4 Timeouts.EtcdAPICall setting, always using a hard‑coded 2‑minute timeout for etcd client calls during cluster bootstrapping.
enrichment.affected: Clusters initialized or joined with kubeadm that specify a custom EtcdAPICall timeout were forced to wait the default 2‑minute timeout, potentially delaying bootstrapping or join operations.
enrichment.fix: The kubeadm code now respects the configured Timeouts.EtcdAPICall value, applying the user‑defined timeout to etcd client operations instead of the default 2 minutes.
enrichment.impact: Users can reliably control etcd call timeouts during kubeadm init/join, avoiding unnecessary wait times and enabling faster failure handling when etcd is unreachable or slow.

enrichment.problem: Not specified
enrichment.affected: Not specified
enrichment.fix: Not specified
enrichment.impact: Not specified

bugOrRegression.description: Added a feature gate `OrderedNamespaceDeletion`. When enabled, the pods resources are deleted before all other resources while namespace deletion to ensure workload security.
bugOrRegression.author: cici37

enrichment.problem: During namespace deletion, resources could be removed before pods, leaving pods running with potentially sensitive data or causing incomplete cleanup, which impacts workload security.
enrichment.affected: Any cluster where namespaces are deleted, especially those with security‑sensitive workloads or policies that rely on pods being the first resource removed.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the `OrderedNamespaceDeletion` feature gate. When enabled, the API server and namespace controller delete pod objects before any other resource in the namespace, guaranteeing that pods are terminated first.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that workloads are securely terminated when a namespace is removed, preventing possible security exposure or orphaned pod behavior. Users can opt‑in via the feature gate for tighter deletion semantics.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a 1.30+ regression in connection stability for exec / attach / portforward requests initiated using a websocket client
bugOrRegression.author: fuweid

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes 1.30 and later, exec, attach, and port‑forward operations that use a websocket client could become unstable or drop the connection, breaking these common debugging and data‑transfer workflows.
enrichment.affected: Anyone using kubectl (or other websocket clients) to exec into, attach to, or port‑forward from pods in clusters running version 1.30 or newer.
enrichment.fix: The regression was fixed so that websocket‑based exec, attach, and port‑forward requests maintain a stable connection again.
enrichment.impact: Restores reliable interactive sessions and port forwarding for developers and operators, allowing normal use of `kubectl exec`, `kubectl attach`, and `kubectl port-forward` without connection drops.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix panic when no UpgradeConfiguration was found in the config file
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: kubeadm panics and crashes during an upgrade when the supplied configuration file does not contain an UpgradeConfiguration section.
enrichment.affected: Administrators running `kubeadm upgrade` with a config file that lacks an UpgradeConfiguration block.
enrichment.fix: Added validation and graceful handling for missing UpgradeConfiguration, preventing the panic and allowing kubeadm to exit with a clear error message.
enrichment.impact: Prevents upgrade commands from unexpectedly terminating, ensuring administrators can diagnose the missing configuration and continue cluster upgrades without downtime.

bugOrRegression.description: Makes kubelet's /metrics/slis endpoint always available
bugOrRegression.author: richabanker

enrichment.problem: The kubelet /metrics/slis endpoint could be unavailable under certain conditions, causing gaps in Service Level Indicator (SLI) data for monitoring systems.
enrichment.affected: Kubelet and any monitoring components that scrape its SLI metrics were affected by intermittent endpoint unavailability.
enrichment.fix: The change ensures the /metrics/slis endpoint is always registered and served by the kubelet, making it consistently reachable for metric collection.
enrichment.impact: Monitoring tools (e.g., Prometheus) can reliably scrape SLI metrics from all kubelets, improving observability and reducing missing data in dashboards and alerts.

bugOrRegression.description: Resolves a performance regression in default 1.31+ configurations, related to the ConsistentListFromCache feature, where rapid create / update API requests across different namespaces encounter increased latency.
bugOrRegression.author: AwesomePatrol

enrichment.problem: A performance regression was introduced in the default 1.31+ configuration. When the ConsistentListFromCache feature is enabled, rapid create and update API requests across different namespaces experience increased latency.
enrichment.affected: Clients and controllers that make rapid create/update API calls across multiple namespaces were seeing slower responses.
enrichment.fix: The regression in the ConsistentListFromCache handling has been fixed, restoring normal request latency for cross‑namespace create/update operations.
enrichment.impact: Reduces API request latency for high‑churn workloads and controllers that issue frequent create/update calls across namespaces, improving overall cluster responsiveness.

other.description: Kubernetes 1.31 is now built with go 1.23
other.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes 1.31 was previously built with an older Go version; the release updates the build toolchain to Go 1.23.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, controller‑manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) are rebuilt with Go 1.23; runtime behavior remains unchanged.
enrichment.fix: The entire Kubernetes codebase is now compiled using Go 1.23, updating all binaries to be built with the newer compiler.
enrichment.impact: Provides up‑to‑date language support, security patches, and potential performance improvements from the newer Go runtime. No functional changes for end users, but improves future maintainability and compatibility.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a bug where kube-apiserver could emit an further watch even even if decryption failed for earlier event and it was not emitted.
bugOrRegression.author: wojtek-t

enrichment.problem: When kube-apiserver failed to decrypt an event during a watch, it could still emit subsequent watch events, leading to missing or out‑of‑order data for clients.
enrichment.affected: Any component that watches encrypted resources via the kube-apiserver (e.g., controllers, operators, and user clients) could see missing or out‑of‑order events.
enrichment.fix: Added logic to stop emitting further watch events after a decryption failure, ensuring that only successfully decrypted events are sent to watch clients.
enrichment.impact: Watch clients (including controllers and custom operators) receive a correct, ordered stream of events even when decryption errors occur, preventing state inconsistency and potential security concerns.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix kubelet restart unmounts volumes of running pods if the referenced PVC is being deleted by the user
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: When the kubelet restarts, it would unmount volumes of pods that are still running if the associated PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) is in the process of being deleted by a user, causing unexpected pod disruptions and potential data loss.
enrichment.affected: Any pod that uses a PVC which is being deleted while the node's kubelet restarts would lose its volume mount, affecting stateful workloads such as databases or applications with persistent storage.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet logic has been updated to correctly handle PVC deletion during a restart, ensuring that volumes for running pods are not unmounted until the pod itself is terminated.
enrichment.impact: Pods with PVCs remain functional across kubelet restarts, preserving data integrity and preventing unnecessary pod restarts or crashes, which improves cluster stability for stateful workloads.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.23.8
feature.author: ameukam

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with an older Go toolchain, lacking recent language security patches and performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) and any clusters that run binaries built from source are affected.
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes components are now compiled using Go 1.23.8, updating the build toolchain across the project.
enrichment.impact: Users receive binaries that incorporate the latest Go security fixes, runtime optimizations, and better forward‑compatibility, reducing potential supply‑chain risk and ensuring smoother builds with newer dependencies.

bugOrRegression.description: Check for newer resize fields when deciding recovery feature's status in kubelet
bugOrRegression.author: gnufied

enrichment.problem: kubelet determined the status of the recovery feature without checking newer volume resize fields, causing it to misinterpret the feature's availability when newer resize APIs were present.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use CSI drivers with volume expansion and rely on kubelet's recovery logic may have experienced incorrect recovery behavior.
enrichment.fix: Implemented a check for the newer resize fields during the recovery feature status decision logic in kubelet, ensuring the correct feature state is used.
enrichment.impact: Correctly reports the recovery feature status, preventing improper handling of volume resize operations during node recovery and improving stability for workloads that depend on CSI volume expansion.

bugOrRegression.description: Resolve a regression introduced in version 1.31 on Windows Proxy, where the creation of HNS endpoints fails if remote HNS endpoints with the same IP address have already been created.
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes v1.31 a regression was introduced in the Windows networking proxy where creating a Host Network Service (HNS) endpoint fails if a remote HNS endpoint with the same IP address already exists. This prevents new pods on Windows nodes from establishing network connectivity in such scenarios.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with Windows nodes using kube-proxy; specifically pods that need to create HNS endpoints when remote endpoints with identical IPs are present.
enrichment.fix: The regression is fixed by correcting the Windows proxy logic so that HNS endpoint creation no longer collides with existing remote endpoints that share the same IP address.
enrichment.impact: Windows workloads that rely on the kube-proxy for networking can once again create pods successfully, restoring expected pod-to-pod and pod-to-service connectivity on clusters with Windows nodes.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built using Go 1.23.10
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes codebase was still built with an older Go version, which could lead to missed security patches, lack of support for newer language features, and potential incompatibilities with newer tooling.
enrichment.affected: Any user building Kubernetes from source will get binaries compiled with Go 1.23.10. The change does not alter functionality for existing clusters but ensures the codebase stays up‑to‑date with the Go ecosystem.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to compile the entire Kubernetes project with Go 1.23.10, bringing all components to the latest supported Go release.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes binaries (kubelet, kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, controller-manager, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) are now built with the newer Go compiler, improving build stability, security, and future compatibility without changing runtime behavior.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built using Go 1.23.9
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: No functional issue was identified; this change updates the Go toolchain used to compile Kubernetes binaries to version 1.23.9.
enrichment.affected: All users of Kubernetes binaries (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) receive components built with the updated Go version.
enrichment.fix: The build process now uses Go 1.23.9, resulting in all Kubernetes components being compiled with the newer compiler and standard library.
enrichment.impact: All clusters running newer Kubernetes releases will use binaries built with Go 1.23.9, which can bring compiler bug fixes, performance improvements, and newer language features while maintaining compatibility.

bugOrRegression.description: Removed a warning around Linux user namespaces and kernel version. If the feature gate `UserNamespacesSupport` was enabled, the kubelet previously warned when detecting a Linux kernel version earlier than 6.3.0. User namespace support on Linux typically does still need kernel 6.3 or newer, but it can work in older kernels too.
bugOrRegression.author: rata

enrichment.problem: When the UserNamespacesSupport feature gate was enabled, kubelet emitted a warning on Linux kernels older than 6.3.0, even though user namespaces can still function on those kernels, causing unnecessary alarm for users.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with kubelet feature gate `UserNamespacesSupport` enabled on nodes running Linux kernels older than 6.3.0.
enrichment.fix: The warning has been removed, so kubelet no longer warns about kernel versions <6.3.0 when UserNamespacesSupport is enabled.
enrichment.impact: Reduces confusion and log noise for users running user namespaces on older kernels, making the feature’s behavior clearer without affecting functionality.

other.description: Improve error message when a pod with user namespaces is created and the runtime doesn't support user namespaces.
other.author: rata

enrichment.problem: Creating a pod that requests user namespaces fails on runtimes that do not support this feature, but the error message was unclear or misleading.
enrichment.affected: Users attempting to create pods with the `UserNamespaces` field on nodes whose container runtime lacks user‑namespace support.
enrichment.fix: The error message emitted when the runtime cannot provide user namespaces has been updated to explicitly state that the runtime does not support user namespaces.
enrichment.impact: Administrators and developers receive a clear, actionable error, making it easier to diagnose why a pod cannot be scheduled with user namespaces and reducing time spent troubleshooting.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a bug causing unexpected delay of creating pods for newly created jobs
bugOrRegression.author: linxiulei

enrichment.problem: When a Job object is created, the controller that creates its Pods experiences a bug that postpones pod creation, leading to unexpected delays before the job starts.
enrichment.affected: Users who create Jobs (batch, CI/CD, data‑processing) experienced delayed pod startup.
enrichment.fix: The bug in the Job controller (part of kube‑controller‑manager) has been corrected so that Pods are instantiated immediately after a new Job is created.
enrichment.impact: Batch and CI/CD workloads that rely on Jobs will start promptly, reducing latency and preventing scheduling back‑logs.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fixed issue where etcd member promotion fails with an error saying the member was already promoted
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: When using kubeadm to promote an etcd member, the operation could fail with an error stating the member was already promoted, even though the promotion had not actually occurred.
enrichment.affected: Clusters managed with kubeadm that need to promote etcd members (e.g., during scaling, recovery, or upgrade operations) were unable to complete the promotion.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now correctly handles the promotion logic, removing the false "already promoted" error and allowing the etcd member to be promoted successfully.
enrichment.impact: Enables reliable etcd member promotion during scaling, recovery, or upgrade workflows, preventing cluster management interruptions and preserving high‑availability guarantees.

securityFixes.title: Nodes can delete themselves by adding an OwnerReference
securityFixes.description: A vulnerability exists in the NodeRestriction admission controller where node users can delete their corresponding node object by patching themselves with an OwnerReference to a cluster-scoped resource. If the OwnerReference resource does not exist or is subsequently deleted, the given node object will be deleted via garbage collection. By default, node users are authorized for create and patch requests but not delete requests against their node object. Since the NodeRestriction admission controller does not prevent patching OwnerReferences, a compromised node could leverage this vulnerability to delete and then recreate its node object with modified taints or labels.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built using Go 1.23.11
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were compiled with an older Go compiler; a newer Go version is required to incorporate security fixes and language improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components built from source (kubelet, kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, controller-manager, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.).
enrichment.fix: The build system was updated to compile all Kubernetes components using Go 1.23.11.
enrichment.impact: Provides security patches, performance gains, and future‑compatibility from the newer Go runtime. No runtime behavior changes for clusters.

bugOrRegression.description: Changed the node restrictions to disallow the node to change it's ownerReferences.
bugOrRegression.author: natherz97

enrichment.problem: Nodes were allowed to modify the ownerReferences field of Kubernetes objects, which could be abused to change object ownership and potentially lead to privilege escalation or disruptive garbage‑collection behavior.
enrichment.affected: Any cluster where a kubelet (node) could issue API requests that modify ownerReferences—typically pods or other resources owned by the node.
enrichment.fix: The node admission restrictions are updated to reject any request from a node that attempts to change an object's ownerReferences, ensuring nodes can only update fields they are authorized for.
enrichment.impact: Prevents nodes from hijacking or deleting resources by altering ownership, improving cluster security and stability for all workloads that rely on proper ownerReference handling.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built using Go 1.23.12
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with an older Go version, lacking recent bug fixes, security patches, and language improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components and any workloads that rely on the Kubernetes binaries (kubelet, kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, controller-manager, kubectl, kube-proxy).
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes components are now compiled with Go 1.23.12, updating the toolchain across the codebase.
enrichment.impact: Provides security and performance improvements from the newer Go runtime, enables use of newer language features, and ensures continued compatibility with future Go releases.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fixed bug where v1beta3's ClusterConfiguration.APIServer.TimeoutForControlPlane is not respected in newer versions of kubeadm where v1beta4 is the default.
bugOrRegression.author: HirazawaUi

enrichment.problem: When using a v1beta3 ClusterConfiguration, the APIServer.TimeoutForControlPlane setting was ignored in newer kubeadm releases where v1beta4 is the default, leading to incorrect timeout behavior during init/join.
enrichment.affected: kubeadm users who set APIServer.TimeoutForControlPlane in a v1beta3 ClusterConfiguration, especially during upgrades to newer kubeadm versions.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm was updated to correctly honor the TimeoutForControlPlane field in v1beta3 configurations even when v1beta4 is the default version.
enrichment.impact: Users upgrading kubeadm or relying on v1beta3 configs now get proper control‑plane timeout handling, preventing unexpected hangs or failures during cluster bootstrap.

other.description: Masked off access to Linux thermal interrupt info in `/proc` and `/sys`.
other.author: saschagrunert

enrichment.problem: Unrestricted read access to Linux thermal interrupt information exposed via /proc and /sys could be leveraged to infer hardware characteristics or perform side‑channel attacks.
enrichment.affected: Any pod or container running on a node that previously could read /proc or /sys thermal interrupt info; node‑level components that expose these files.
enrichment.fix: Kubernetes now masks (removes) the thermal interrupt entries from /proc and /sys for containers/nodes, preventing processes from reading this information.
enrichment.impact: Reduces the attack surface on nodes, improving cluster security. Workloads or monitoring tools that relied on these thermal interrupt files will no longer see them and may need alternative methods.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built using Go 1.24.9

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, requiring updates to the build environment.
enrichment.affected: Anyone building Kubernetes from source, including maintainers, CI systems, and custom build environments.
enrichment.fix: The build process now uses Go 1.24.9, updating the compiler and standard library for all components.
enrichment.impact: Developers and CI pipelines must use Go 1.24.9 or later to build Kubernetes; the newer compiler may bring security patches, performance improvements, and future compatibility.

feature.description: update setcap and debian-base to bookworm-v1.0.6
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Not specified (the release updates the setcap utility and the Debian base image to the newer bookworm-v1.0.6 version).
enrichment.affected: Build pipelines, CI jobs, and any users relying on the Kubernetes build images that incorporate setcap or the Debian base.
enrichment.fix: Upgrade the setcap package and the debian-base image used in Kubernetes build and test pipelines to bookworm-v1.0.6, bringing in upstream security patches and newer OS packages.
enrichment.impact: Images built from the Kubernetes source now contain newer, patched binaries and OS libraries, reducing potential security exposure and improving compatibility for downstream users and CI systems.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix Windows kube-proxy to prevent intermittent deletion of ClusterIP load balancers in HNS when internalTrafficPolicy=Local, ensuring stable service connectivity.
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: On Windows nodes, kube-proxy could intermittently delete ClusterIP load balancers managed by HNS when a Service has internalTrafficPolicy=Local, causing loss of connectivity to those services.
enrichment.affected: Windows workloads using Services with internalTrafficPolicy=Local; clusters where kube-proxy runs on Windows nodes.
enrichment.fix: Updated the Windows kube-proxy implementation to correctly handle ClusterIP load balancer objects in HNS, preventing their unintended deletion when internalTrafficPolicy=Local is set.
enrichment.impact: Ensures stable service connectivity for Windows workloads that rely on ClusterIP services with internalTrafficPolicy=Local, reducing unexpected service outages.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fixes a preflight check that can fail hostname construction in IPV6 setups
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: Kubeadm preflight check fails when constructing the hostname on IPv6-only setups, causing init/join to abort.
enrichment.affected: Clusters being set up with kubeadm on IPv6 networks; administrators attempting kubeadm init or join in IPv6 environments.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the hostname construction logic in the preflight check to correctly handle IPv6 addresses, allowing the check to succeed.
enrichment.impact: Users can now bootstrap and join IPv6 clusters with kubeadm without encountering preflight failures, improving reliability for IPv6 deployments.

other.description: Kubeadm: updated the supported etcd version to v3.5.24 for the skewed control plane version v1.33.
other.author: hakman

enrichment.problem: Kubeadm did not list etcd version v3.5.24 as supported for a control plane version v1.33, leading to potential incompatibility warnings or failures when initializing or upgrading clusters with that combination.
enrichment.affected: Users employing kubeadm to bootstrap or upgrade clusters with a v1.33 control plane and etcd versions other than v3.5.24 would previously encounter compatibility problems.
enrichment.fix: The supported etcd version list in kubeadm was updated to include v3.5.24 for the skewed control plane version v1.33, allowing the combination to be used without errors.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators can now safely create or upgrade clusters with kubeadm using etcd v3.5.24 and control plane v1.33, avoiding compatibility issues and ensuring smooth upgrades.
